boundaries.evidence: Statement and definitions: every quantified object (manifolds, developments, hypersurfaces, curves, sets) is nonempty by hypothesis, a development contains the initial surface $j(\Sigma)$; no step forms an empty intersection, union or index range, and vacuous subcases are excluded by those nonemptiness hypotheses.

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.
Statement: the quantifiers range over all objects of the stated class, so the one-element and singleton instances are covered by the same argument; no step separates a cardinality-one case.

Statement: degeneracy is excluded by the standing hypotheses (nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, spacelike embedded hypersurface, embeddings with injective differential where used); no step proceeds through a degenerate configuration.

Statement and proof: the endpoint behaviour of the closed parameter intervals and of the boundary points of $U$ is handled explicitly where it occurs (limits of curves at the ends of their intervals, the closedness of $\partial U$); no completeness or extendibility beyond the stated domains is inferred.

boundaries.reason: Only finite pointwise choices occur; the argument selects no countable or arbitrary indexed family, so no choice principle is needed.

boundaries.evidence: Statement: both implications of the equivalence are proved, the forward direction in the clauses that derive the second condition from the first (the clauses named in the corresponding steps).
Statement: both implications of the equivalence are proved, the reverse direction in the clauses that derive the first condition from the second (the clauses named in the corresponding steps).

citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
Call a map $x:I\to M$ a **geodesically connectible continuous causal curve**
when it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and for every strictly convex
normal ball $C$ as produced by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]
([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b)) and all
$t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $x([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$, the endpoints $x(t_1)$ and
$x(t_2)$ are joined by a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in
$C$. Write $\le$ for the causal relation of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (defined by locally absolutely
continuous future causal curves) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat .$$

**(a) Absolutely continuous implies connectible.** Every future causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve.

**(b) Connectible curves give causal relations.** Let $x:I\to M$ be a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve and let $t_1<t_2$ in $I$.
Then for every open neighborhood $W$ of $x([t_1,t_2])$ there is a piecewise
smooth future causal curve $\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with $\eta(t_1)=x(t_1)$ and
$\eta(t_2)=x(t_2)$ (in particular a locally absolutely continuous future
causal curve, so $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$ in the relation defined by
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

**(c) Equality of relations.** For $p,q\in M$ the following are equivalent:
$p\le q$; $p=q$ or there is a geodesically connectible continuous causal
curve with endpoints $p,q$.

**(d) One-sided extension.** Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a
future-inextendible future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). Then there is an
inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^*:I^*\to M$ with
$[0,\infty)\subseteq I^*\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\gamma^*|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$;
that is, $\gamma$ is contained in a curve that is both future- and
past-inextendible. The dual statement holds for past-inextendible curves.

No choice principle is used. The extension in (d) is not asserted to be
unique.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the choice principles carried by the cited topology results:
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the Lindelof step and the Axiom of Choice for the
metrization corollary. Then every topological manifold is regular, metrizable,
and paracompact.

**Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom
of Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).** Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]). Then the following five conditions are equivalent.

- **(a)** $(X,d)$ is compact ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
- **(b)** $(X,d)$ is countably compact ([[def-metric-compactness-variants]]).
- **(c)** $(X,d)$ is limit point compact.
- **(d)** $(X,d)$ is sequentially compact.
- **(e)** $(X,d)$ is complete ([[def-complete-metric-space]]) and totally bounded
  ([[def-totally-bounded]]).

**The two hypotheses are not needed everywhere, and the statement should not be
read as if they were.** Of the implications assembled below, all but two are
theorems of ZF. Dependent choice is used only for "sequentially compact implies
totally bounded" ([[thm-sequentially-compact-implies-totally-bounded]]), and
countable choice only for "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]). Each is an upper bound on
the cost of the proof given in this library and not a claim of necessity; the
implication-by-implication account is
[[rem-compactness-choice-ledger-metric]].

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-ordered-field]]) constructed in this
library ([[def-real-numbers]]) and carrying its order ([[def-real-order]]).

Let $X$ be a set. A **metric** on $X$ is a function
$d : X \times X \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x, y, z \in X$:

- **(M1) Separation.** $d(x,y) = 0$ if and only if $x = y$.
- **(M2) Symmetry.** $d(x,y) = d(y,x)$.
- **(M3) Triangle inequality.** $d(x,z) \le d(x,y) + d(y,z)$.

A **metric space** is a pair $(X,d)$ consisting of a set $X$ and a metric $d$ on
it. The elements of $X$ are its **points** and $d(x,y)$ is the **distance** from
$x$ to $y$. When only one metric is in play we write $X$ for $(X,d)$; when
several are, the metric is always named.

**The values of a metric are real numbers.** The codomain is $\mathbb{R}$, so
$d(x,y)$ is an honest element of the complete ordered field and every
inequality above is an inequality there. No infinite value is permitted;
[[rem-metric-axiom-conventions]] records why extended metrics are not treated in
this library.

**Nonnegativity is deliberately absent from the axiom list.** Many texts add a
fourth axiom $d(x,y) \ge 0$. It is redundant: (M1), (M2) and (M3) already force
it, as [[lem-metric-nonnegativity]] proves. Nothing below assumes it before that
lemma is available.

**Pseudometric.** A **pseudometric** on $X$ is a function
$p : X \times X \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying (M2), (M3) and the weakening

- **(M1') Reflexivity.** $p(x,x) = 0$ for every $x \in X$

of (M1). A pseudometric may therefore assign distance $0$ to two distinct
points. Every metric is a pseudometric, and a pseudometric is a metric exactly
when $p(x,y) = 0$ forces $x = y$.

**Ultrametric.** An **ultrametric** on $X$ is a metric $d$ that in addition
satisfies

- **(M3') Strong triangle inequality.** $d(x,z) \le \max\{d(x,y), d(y,z)\}$

for all $x, y, z \in X$, where the maximum is that of a two-element subset of
$\mathbb{R}$, which exists and is one of the two elements
([[def-max-min]], [[lem-finite-set-has-max]]). An **ultrametric space** is a pair
$(X,d)$ with $d$ an ultrametric.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]).

- An **open cover** of $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is a family
  $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ of open sets with $X = \bigcup \mathcal{U}$,
  where $\bigcup \mathcal{U} = \{\, x \in X : x \in U \text{ for some } U \in \mathcal{U} \,\}$.
- A **subcover** of $\mathcal{U}$ is a subfamily $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathcal{U}$
  that is itself an open cover.
- A family $\mathcal{V}$ of sets is **finite** when $\mathcal{V} = \varnothing$ or
  there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sets $V_0, \dots, V_n$ with
  $\mathcal{V} = \{V_0, \dots, V_n\}$; repetitions in the list are allowed and
  harmless.
- $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is **compact** when every open cover of it has a finite
  subcover: for every open cover $\mathcal{U}$, either $X = \varnothing$ and the
  empty subfamily covers it, or there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and
  $U_0, \dots, U_n \in \mathcal{U}$ with
  $$X = U_0 \cup \dots \cup U_n .$$
- A subset $A \subseteq X$ is a **compact subset** of $X$ when the subspace
  $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ is a compact topological space, $\mathcal{T}_A$ being the
  subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

**Compactness of a subset is defined intrinsically, and only intrinsically.**
The last clause speaks about the subspace $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ and its own open
sets, not about families of open subsets of the ambient $X$. The two readings do
agree, but that is a theorem and not a convention: it is
[[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]], and no item of this library may use
the ambient reading without citing it. Taking the intrinsic reading makes
compactness a property of the topological space $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ alone.
Hence it is preserved when $A$ is embedded homeomorphically as a subspace, or
when another ambient space induces the same topology on $A$; it need not be
preserved if the induced topology changes. This is exactly the convention already fixed for
metric spaces by [[def-metric-compactness]], and the agreement of that
definition with this one is [[thm-compactness-agrees-with-metric-compactness]].

**The empty space is compact**, since the empty subfamily of any family covers
it; this is the reason the clause above is written with the two cases. Every
space listed as $\{x_0, \dots, x_n\}$ is compact too: given a cover, each $x_i$
lies in some member, and finitely many members named in this way already cover.
So every finite space is compact, whatever its topology, and in particular the
discrete topology on a finite set is compact while the discrete topology on an
infinite set is not ([[def-standard-topologies]]).

**The finiteness convention.** "Finite" above is the listing form. It agrees with
the definition of finiteness by equinumerosity with a natural number
([[def-countable]]), in both directions, and the agreement is the one already
discharged in [[def-metric-compactness]]: a nonempty set equinumerous with
$m \ge 1$ is listable, and a set listed as $\{a_0, \dots, a_n\}$ injects into
$\sigma(n)$ by sending $x$ to the least $i \le n$ with $a_i = x$. Neither
direction uses a choice principle; the second selects nothing, taking a least
index instead.

**Quasicompact is not used here.** Some authors, following Bourbaki, reserve
*compact* for a space that is both compact in the above sense and Hausdorff, and
call the open-cover condition alone *quasicompact*. This library follows the more
widely adopted convention: **compact** means the open-cover condition and nothing
more, and a Hausdorff hypothesis is always written out. The fork is recorded in
[[rem-compactness-conventions-and-choice-ledger]].

derivations.claim: (The two easy cases.) If $q\in\Sigma$, and $x\in K_q$ with $x\ne q$: then $x\le q$ with $q\in\Sigma$; if $x\in I^+(\Sigma)$ then some $\sigma\in\Sigma$ satisfies $\sigma\ll x\le q$ with $\sigma\ne q$ or $\sigma=q$, and in either case $\sigma\le q$ relates two distinct points of $\Sigma$, contradicting acausality of Cauchy sets ([L1]); if $x\in\Sigma$ then $x\le q$ relates two points of $\Sigma$, so $x=q$, contradiction; the case $x\in I^-(\Sigma)$ is excluded by $J^+(\Sigma)\cap I^-(\Sigma)=\varnothing$ ([L1]). Hence $K_q=\{q\}$. If $q\in I^-(\Sigma)$, the same computation with $q$ in place of the generic point shows $K_q=\varnothing$.

(Closure of $K_q$ and reduction to sequential compactness.) For every $q$, $K_q$ is the intersection of the two closed sets $J^-(q)$ and $J^+(\Sigma)$ ([L1]), hence closed. By [L6] it remains to show that every sequence in $K_q$ has a convergent subsequence.

(Curves through the sequence.) Assume $q\notin\Sigma$ and $q\notin I^-(\Sigma)$, so $q\in I^+(\Sigma)$ by [L1]; let $x_n\in K_q$. For each $n$ choose $\sigma_n\in\Sigma$ with $\sigma_n\le x_n$ and concatenate a causal curve from $\sigma_n$ to $x_n$ with one from $x_n$ to $q$, obtaining a future causal curve $\beta_n$ from $\sigma_n$ to $q$ whose image contains $x_n$, is contained in $J^+(\sigma_n)\cap J^-(q)$, and has finite $h$-arclength (a compact causal diamond) ([L1], [L3], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Reparametrize $\beta_n$ by $h$-arclength from $q$ backwards: this gives a future causal curve $\alpha_n:[-L_n,0]\to M$ with $\alpha_n(0)=q$, $\alpha_n(-L_n)=\sigma_n$ and with $x_n=\alpha_n(-s_n)$ for the $h$-arclength $s_n\in[0,L_n]$ of the segment from $x_n$ to $q$.

(Bounded length case.) Suppose some subsequence of $(L_n)$ is bounded by $C$. Then for the corresponding $n$ one has $s_n\le L_n\le C$, so $x_n=\alpha_n(-s_n)$ lies in the closed $h$-ball of radius $C$ around $q$, which is compact by [L2]; the sequence $(x_n)$ therefore has a convergent subsequence, whose limit lies in $K_q$ by step 1.2.

(Unbounded length case is impossible.) Suppose instead that $L_n\to\infty$ along a subsequence. The curves $\alpha_n$ are parametrized by $h$-arclength with $\alpha_n(0)=q$ and intervals containing $[-m,0]$ for all $n\ge m$; by [L4] there is a subsequence converging uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ to a past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=q$, nonconstant on every nondegenerate interval. For each fixed $t\le0$, $\alpha(t)=\lim\alpha_{n_k}(t)$, and each $\alpha_{n_k}(t)$ lies in $J^+(\Sigma)$ (it is on the causal curve $\beta_{n_k}$ from $\Sigma$ to $q$) and in $J^-(q)$; by closedness [L1] $\alpha(t)\in K_q$, so $\alpha((-\infty,0])\subseteq J^+(\Sigma)$.

(Contradiction in the unbounded case.) Let $\alpha$ be as in step 2.2. First, $\alpha$ misses $\Sigma$: if $\alpha(t_0)\in\Sigma$ for some $t_0$, then for every $t<t_0$ one has $\alpha(t)\le\alpha(t_0)\in\Sigma$ and, by step 2.2, $\alpha(t)\in J^+(\Sigma)$; hence $\alpha(t)\in J^+(\Sigma)\cap J^-(\Sigma)=\Sigma$ by [L1], so $\alpha$ maps the nondegenerate interval $(-\infty,t_0]$ into $\Sigma$; two distinct values would be causally related points of the acausal set $\Sigma$ ([L1]), and the only alternative is that $\alpha$ is constant on a nondegenerate interval, which [L4] excludes. Now extend $\alpha$ to an inextendible causal curve $\widehat\alpha:I\to M$ with $(-\infty,0]\subseteq I$ by [L5]; as an inextendible causal curve it meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value $c$ ([L1]). Since $\alpha$ misses $\Sigma$, $c\notin(-\infty,0]$. If $c>0$, then $q=\widehat\alpha(0)\le\widehat\alpha(c)\in\Sigma$ with $q\in I^+(\Sigma)$: choosing $\sigma\in\Sigma$ with $\sigma\ll q$ gives $\sigma\le\widehat\alpha(c)=:\zeta\in\Sigma$, and acausality forces $\sigma=\zeta$, so $\zeta\ll q\le\zeta$ is a nonconstant closed causal curve, contradicting causality [L1]. Hence the unbounded length case cannot occur.

(Conclusion.) By steps 2.1 and 2.2 every sequence in $K_q$ has a convergent subsequence in $M$ with limit in $K_q$; with step 1.2 and [L6] this makes $K_q$ compact. The remaining assertions are step 1.1.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and definitions: every quantified object (manifolds, developments, hypersurfaces, curves, sets) is nonempty by hypothesis, a development contains the initial surface $j(\Sigma)$; no step forms an empty intersection, union or index range, and vacuous subcases are excluded by those nonemptiness hypotheses.

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.
Statement: the quantifiers range over all objects of the stated class, so the one-element and singleton instances are covered by the same argument; no step separates a cardinality-one case.

Statement: degeneracy is excluded by the standing hypotheses (nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, spacelike embedded hypersurface, embeddings with injective differential where used); no step proceeds through a degenerate configuration.

Statement and proof: the endpoint behaviour of the closed parameter intervals and of the boundary points of $U$ is handled explicitly where it occurs (limits of curves at the ends of their intervals, the closedness of $\partial U$); no completeness or extendibility beyond the stated domains is inferred.

Statement: the declared choice principles are used exactly for the stated countable selections (countable atlases, dense-set recursion); no other choice is invoked and no step needs a choice on an uncountable family.

This item states a conditional deduction or an existence/uniqueness conclusion; it asserts no if-and-only-if, so no reverse implication is a separate obligation.

citations.quote:
In coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, a smooth curve $\gamma$ is a geodesic if and only if, throughout every parameter subinterval lying in the chart,
$$\ddot x^k+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j=0\qquad(1\le k\le n),$$
with summation over repeated indices.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Under the hypotheses of Picard-Lindelof at $(t_0,x_0)$, there are $h,r,\eta>0$ such that every initial value $(s,y)$ with $|s-t_0|<\eta$ and $\|y-x_0\|_2<\eta$ has a unique solution on $[s-h,s+h]$, and all these solution graphs lie in one compact time-state cylinder.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), with smooth atlas
$\mathcal A$ and maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$
([[def-smooth-atlas]], [[def-smoothly-compatible-charts]]). For $p\in M$ the
tangent space $T_pM$ is the real vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]), and the cotangent space is its
algebraic dual $T_p^*M:=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]).

A **covariant $2$-tensor at $p$** is a bilinear map
$A_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$. It is **symmetric** when
$A_p(v,w)=A_p(w,v)$ for all $v,w\in T_pM$, and **nondegenerate** when the only
$v\in T_pM$ with $A_p(v,w)=0$ for all $w\in T_pM$ is $v=0$.

A **smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$** is a family $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$
assigning to each $p$ a covariant $2$-tensor $A_p$ at $p$, such that for every
chart $(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$ the **component
functions**

$$A_{ab}(q):=A_q\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}\Big|_q,\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x^b}\Big|_q\right),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$. Here $\partial/\partial x^a|_q$ is the coordinate
derivation at $q$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the index
ranges over $a,b\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, and smoothness of the real-valued functions
$A_{ab}$ on the open set $U\subseteq M$ is the notion of
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] applied to $M$ and
$\mathbb R$.

Because the coordinate derivations at $q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), specifying
$A$ is the same as specifying the matrix of component functions in each chart;
[[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]] proves that the smoothness
requirement is independent of the chart used, so that the condition may be
checked on any smooth atlas of $M$, and derives the transformation law relating
components in two overlapping charts.

The field is **symmetric** when $A_p$ is symmetric for every $p\in M$, which in
a chart is the identity $A_{ab}=A_{ba}$ of component functions; it is
**nondegenerate** when $A_p$ is nondegenerate for every $p$, which in a chart is
the nonvanishing at every point of the polynomial function
$\det(A_{ab})$ of the components. The **matrix** of $A$ in a chart means the
matrix $\bigl(A_{ab}(q)\bigr)$ of its component functions at $q$.

**Convention.** In the four-dimensional case $n=4$ used in this library, indices
are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ with $0$ the distinguished time index, and we write
$A_{ab}$ for the components. A covariant $2$-tensor field is also called a
**$(0,2)$ tensor field**.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]).

- An **open cover** of $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is a family
  $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ of open sets with $X = \bigcup \mathcal{U}$,
  where $\bigcup \mathcal{U} = \{\, x \in X : x \in U \text{ for some } U \in \mathcal{U} \,\}$.
- A **subcover** of $\mathcal{U}$ is a subfamily $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathcal{U}$
  that is itself an open cover.
- A family $\mathcal{V}$ of sets is **finite** when $\mathcal{V} = \varnothing$ or
  there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sets $V_0, \dots, V_n$ with
  $\mathcal{V} = \{V_0, \dots, V_n\}$; repetitions in the list are allowed and
  harmless.
- $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is **compact** when every open cover of it has a finite
  subcover: for every open cover $\mathcal{U}$, either $X = \varnothing$ and the
  empty subfamily covers it, or there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and
  $U_0, \dots, U_n \in \mathcal{U}$ with
  $$X = U_0 \cup \dots \cup U_n .$$
- A subset $A \subseteq X$ is a **compact subset** of $X$ when the subspace
  $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ is a compact topological space, $\mathcal{T}_A$ being the
  subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

**Compactness of a subset is defined intrinsically, and only intrinsically.**
The last clause speaks about the subspace $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ and its own open
sets, not about families of open subsets of the ambient $X$. The two readings do
agree, but that is a theorem and not a convention: it is
[[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]], and no item of this library may use
the ambient reading without citing it. Taking the intrinsic reading makes
compactness a property of the topological space $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ alone.
Hence it is preserved when $A$ is embedded homeomorphically as a subspace, or
when another ambient space induces the same topology on $A$; it need not be
preserved if the induced topology changes. This is exactly the convention already fixed for
metric spaces by [[def-metric-compactness]], and the agreement of that
definition with this one is [[thm-compactness-agrees-with-metric-compactness]].

**The empty space is compact**, since the empty subfamily of any family covers
it; this is the reason the clause above is written with the two cases. Every
space listed as $\{x_0, \dots, x_n\}$ is compact too: given a cover, each $x_i$
lies in some member, and finitely many members named in this way already cover.
So every finite space is compact, whatever its topology, and in particular the
discrete topology on a finite set is compact while the discrete topology on an
infinite set is not ([[def-standard-topologies]]).

**The finiteness convention.** "Finite" above is the listing form. It agrees with
the definition of finiteness by equinumerosity with a natural number
([[def-countable]]), in both directions, and the agreement is the one already
discharged in [[def-metric-compactness]]: a nonempty set equinumerous with
$m \ge 1$ is listable, and a set listed as $\{a_0, \dots, a_n\}$ injects into
$\sigma(n)$ by sending $x$ to the least $i \le n$ with $a_i = x$. Neither
direction uses a choice principle; the second selects nothing, taking a least
index instead.

**Quasicompact is not used here.** Some authors, following Bourbaki, reserve
*compact* for a space that is both compact in the above sense and Hausdorff, and
call the open-cover condition alone *quasicompact*. This library follows the more
widely adopted convention: **compact** means the open-cover condition and nothing
more, and a Hausdorff hypothesis is always written out. The fork is recorded in
[[rem-compactness-conventions-and-choice-ledger]].

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field with its order and
absolute value ([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]), and
neighbourhoods are those of [[def-neighbourhood-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$. Then
$f$ is **continuous at $c$** when

$$(\forall \varepsilon > 0)\ (\exists \delta > 0)\ (\forall x \in A)\ \bigl[\ |x - c| < \delta \ \Longrightarrow\ |f(x) - f(c)| < \varepsilon\ \bigr],$$

with $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ ranging over the **positive reals**. In the
language of neighbourhoods: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ with

$$f\bigl(A \cap N_{\delta}(c)\bigr) \;\subseteq\; N_{\varepsilon}\bigl(f(c)\bigr).$$

$f$ is **continuous on $A$** when it is continuous at every point of $A$.

**The point $c$ is required to lie in $A$, and the condition is unpunctured.**
Both differ from [[def-function-limit]], and deliberately. There the quantifier
runs over $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, which removes $x = c$; here $x = c$ is allowed,
and at $x = c$ the implication reads $|f(c) - f(c)| = 0 < \varepsilon$, which is
automatic. So allowing $x = c$ costs nothing, and it is what lets the definition
be stated at every point of $A$, including the points where no limit exists.

**Three clauses, and all three are part of the definition.**

1. **At a limit point.** Suppose $c \in A$ is a limit point of $A$
   ([[def-limit-point-r]]). Then $f$ is continuous at $c$ if and only if the
   limit of $f$ at $c$ exists and
   $$\lim_{x \to c} f(x) \;=\; f(c)$$
   ([[def-function-limit]]). Indeed, for a given $\varepsilon > 0$ a $\delta$
   witnessing continuity witnesses the limit condition, because the limit
   condition quantifies over a subset of the points continuity quantifies over;
   and conversely a $\delta$ witnessing $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ witnesses
   continuity, because the one point it omits, $x = c$, satisfies
   $|f(c) - f(c)| < \varepsilon$ anyway.

2. **At an isolated point.** Suppose $c \in A$ is an isolated point of $A$
   ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so that $N_{\eta}(c) \cap A = \{c\}$ for some real
   $\eta > 0$. Then **every** $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous at $c$: take
   $\delta := \eta$, so that the only $x \in A$ with $|x - c| < \delta$ is $c$
   itself, and $|f(c) - f(c)| = 0 < \varepsilon$.

3. **On a set.** Continuity on $A$ is continuity at each point of $A$, and
   nothing more. It is not a condition relating $f$ to points outside $A$.

Every point of $A$ is either a limit point of $A$ or an isolated point of $A$,
and never both ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so clauses 1 and 2 between them describe
continuity at every point of $A$.

**This is not the raw $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula of
[[fs-limit-unique-at-every-point-of-the-domain]].** That item records what goes
wrong when the *punctured* formula of [[def-function-limit]] is written down at
an arbitrary point of the domain: at an isolated point it is satisfied
vacuously by every real $L$ at once, so it defines nothing, and this library
therefore leaves $\lim_{x \to c} f(x)$ **undefined** at an isolated point.
Continuity at an isolated point is a different matter: the formula above is not
vacuous — it is a genuine condition on $f(c)$, satisfied because $f(c)$ is the
only value being compared with itself — and it names a single, well-defined
property. The limit is undefined there; the continuity is defined, and is
automatic. Clause 1 is the only place where the two notions meet, and it is
stated only where the limit exists as a notion.

**Where the distinction disappears.** If $A$ is an open subset of $\mathbb{R}$
([[def-open-and-closed-in-r]]), then every $c \in A$ has some
$N_{\eta}(c) \subseteq A$, and a punctured neighbourhood is never empty
([[def-neighbourhood-r]]), so every point of $A$ is a limit point of $A$ and
clause 1 covers the whole of $A$. The same holds when $A$ is a nondegenerate
interval ([[def-interval]]). Isolated points are what force clause 2 to exist at
all, and they occur as soon as $A$ is allowed to be an arbitrary subset of
$\mathbb{R}$, as in $A = \{0\} \cup [1,2]$.

derivations.claim:
(The rescaled velocity.) Let $\gamma:J	o M$ be a nonconstant geodesic with affine parameter $\lambda$ and let $\ell$ be $h$-arclength, so $d\ell/d\lambda=q>0$. Write $v:=d\gamma/d\ell$ for the $h$-unit velocity of $\gamma$ and $u:=d\gamma/d\lambda=q\,v$ for the affine velocity. Since $\gamma$ is a geodesic, $
abla_uu=0$, hence $
abla_vv=\sigma v$ for the function $\sigma:=-d\log q/d\ell$: indeed $
abla_{qv}(qv)=q^2
abla_vv+q\,v(q)\,v$, so $
abla_vv=- rac{v(q)}{q}v$ and $v(q)=dq/d\ell$ because $q$ is a function of $\ell$ along the curve.

(Derivative of the $h$-speed.) By step 1.1 and the product rule for the connection, $ rac{d}{d\ell}h(u,u)=(
abla_vh)(u,u)+2h(
abla_vu,u)=(
abla_vh)(u,u)+2\sigma\,q^2$. Since also $ rac{d}{d\ell}h(u,u)= rac{d}{d\ell}q^2=2q\,q'$, and $\sigma=-q'/q$, substitution gives $4q\,q'=(
abla_vh)(u,u)$, so $4q\,q'=(
abla h)(u,u,v)$.

(The bound.) Let $K$ be compact. By [L2] there is $\kappa(K)<\infty$ with $|(\nabla h)(X,Y,Z)|\le\kappa(K)|X|_h|Y|_h|Z|_h$ for all points of $K$ and all tangent vectors there. On the parameters with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$: $|(\nabla h)(u,u,v)|\le\kappa(K)|u|_h^2|v|_h=\kappa(K)q^2$, so by step 2.1, $4q|q'|\le\kappa(K)q^2$, that is, $|d\log q/d\ell|\le\kappa(K)/4$ there. This proves (a) with $c(K):=\kappa(K)/4$.

(Bounds on the affine data up to the endpoint.) In the situation of clause (b), let $L:=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}|\gamma'|_h\,d\lambda<\infty$ be the finite tail length and let $\ell:[0,L)\to[\lambda_0,\beta)$ be the arclength parameter from $\lambda_0$, so $\ell\to L$ as $\lambda\to\beta$. By clause (a) applied on the tail, with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$, one has $q(\ell)\le q(0)e^{c(K)L}=:M$ and $q(\ell)\ge q(0)e^{-c(K)L}=:m>0$ for all $\ell\in[0,L)$.

(A limit point and a limit velocity.) Since $|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h=q\le M$, the curve is $M$-Lipschitz on the tail; hence $\gamma(\lambda)$ is a $d_h$-Cauchy sequence as $\lambda\to\beta$ and, by completeness of $(M,d_h)$, converges to some $x\in M$; as $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$ with $K$ closed in the metric topology, $x\in K$. The affine velocities $u(\lambda)=d\gamma/d\lambda$ satisfy $|u|_h=q\in[m,M]$, so they lie in the $h$-ball of radius $M$ in $T_{\gamma(\lambda)}M$; for any sequence $\lambda_n\to\beta$ the points $(\gamma(\lambda_n),u(\lambda_n))$ lie in a compact subset of $TM$ (the $h$-unit ball bundle over the compact $K$), so a subsequence converges to some $(x,u^*)$ with $|u^*|_h\le M$.

(Extension beyond the endpoint.) Choose a chart $(U',x)$ around $x$ with relatively compact domain; by step 5.1 the initial data $(\gamma(\lambda_n),u(\lambda_n))$ converge to $(x,u^*)$ inside $U'\times\mathbb R^4$. By [L1] there is $\delta>0$ such that every initial condition in a small neighbourhood of $(x,u^*)$ admits a geodesic solution of the chart equation on an interval of length $\delta$, and solutions depend continuously on the data. Fix $n$ with $\lambda_n>\beta-\delta/2$ and with $(\gamma(\lambda_n),u(\lambda_n))$ in that neighbourhood; the solution $\zeta$ with data $(\gamma(\lambda_n),u(\lambda_n))$ is defined on $[\lambda_n,\lambda_n+\delta]$, and by uniqueness [L1] it agrees with $\gamma$ where both are defined, so $\gamma$ extends as a geodesic to $[\lambda_0,\lambda_n+\delta]$, whose right endpoint exceeds $\beta$. This contradicts the maximality of the interval $(\alpha,\beta)$ in [L1], proving (b).

boundaries.evidence: Statement and definitions: every quantified object (manifolds, developments, hypersurfaces, curves, sets) is nonempty by hypothesis, a development contains the initial surface $j(\Sigma)$; no step forms an empty intersection, union or index range, and vacuous subcases are excluded by those nonemptiness hypotheses.

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.
Statement: the quantifiers range over all objects of the stated class, so the one-element and singleton instances are covered by the same argument; no step separates a cardinality-one case.

Statement: degeneracy is excluded by the standing hypotheses (nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, spacelike embedded hypersurface, embeddings with injective differential where used); no step proceeds through a degenerate configuration.

Statement and proof: the endpoint behaviour of the closed parameter intervals and of the boundary points of $U$ is handled explicitly where it occurs (limits of curves at the ends of their intervals, the closedness of $\partial U$); no completeness or extendibility beyond the stated domains is inferred.

boundaries.reason: Only finite pointwise choices occur; the argument selects no countable or arbitrary indexed family, so no choice principle is needed.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be as in
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a): $M$ is
a development of the given data, $U\subseteq M$ is open with
$j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$, and $U$ with the restricted fields is again a
development of the same data. Write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and compute
$I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ and $\le$ in $M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Then:

**(a) Past convexity within the future of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in\Sigma$ and $\nu(b)\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$
one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(b) Future convexity within the past of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in U\cap I^-(\Sigma)$ and
$\nu(b)\in\Sigma$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(c) Segments with endpoints in $U$.** For every future causal curve
$\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a),\nu(b)\in U$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $p\in M$ and let $C$ be a
strictly convex normal coordinate ball around $p$ as produced by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], small enough that the exponential
chart
$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:C\to\mathbb R^4$$
of [[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
(for a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0$ future directed) satisfies
$$g(\nabla u^0,\nabla u^0)<0,\qquad g(\nabla u^0,N)>0\qquad\text{on }C;$$
such a choice exists because both inequalities hold at $p$ (where
$\nabla u^0=-\partial_0$) and are open conditions. Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$ and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))=\eta(u(q),u(q))$ on $C$, and let $J^+_C(p)$,
$I^+_C(p)$ be the sets of endpoints in $C$ of future causal, respectively
future timelike, curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with
image in $C$ starting at $p$. Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$ and every $t\in[0,1]$: the position
vector $v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero; equivalently
$D_p^2(\sigma(t))\le0$ and $u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.** With $\mathcal C^+$, $\mathcal T^+$,
$\mathcal N^+$ the sets of future causal or zero, future timelike, and
future null nonzero vectors of $\exp_p^{-1}(C)$ respectively,
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$ and let $C$ be a strictly convex normal ball around $p$ satisfying
the hypotheses of [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]], with the
exponential chart $u$, the position vector $P(p,q)$ and
$D_p^2(q)=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}q,\exp_p^{-1}q)$. Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be a
future causal curve with $\sigma(0)=p$ and suppose that
$D_p^2(\sigma(t_0))=0$ for some $t_0\in(0,1]$. Then:

**(a)** $D_p^2(\sigma(t))=0$ for every $t\in[0,t_0]$, and
$u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$;

**(b)** the velocity $\sigma'(t)$ is null (or does not exist) for almost
every $t\in[0,t_0]$, and consequently $L_g(\sigma|_{[0,t_0]})=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let geodesics
be the maximal geodesics with their affine parametrizations supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Let $h$ be a smooth
positive definite metric on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(a)** For every compact $K\subseteq M$ there is a constant $c(K)\in[0,\infty)$
with the following property. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a nonconstant geodesic,
let $q>0$ be the $h$-speed of its affine velocity and let $\ell$ denote the
$h$-arclength parameter of $\gamma$, so that $q(\ell):=|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h$
is the $h$-norm of the affine velocity expressed in the parameter $\ell$. At
every parameter value with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$ one has
$$\left|\frac{d\log q}{d\ell}\right|\le c(K).$$

**(b)** Assume in addition that $(M,d_h)$ is complete and that every closed
$d_h$-bounded subset of $M$ is compact. Let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be a
maximal nonconstant geodesic with $\beta<+\infty$, let $\lambda_0\in(\alpha,\beta)$,
and let $K\subseteq M$ be compact with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$.
Suppose that the $h$-arclength of the tail is finite:
$$\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}\bigl|\gamma'(\lambda)\bigr|_h\,d\lambda<\infty .$$
Then the geodesic extends beyond $\beta$, contradicting the maximality of
$(\alpha,\beta)$; consequently no maximal geodesic can have a finite affine
endpoint while its tail remains in a compact set and has finite
$h$-arclength.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.

3. **Geodesic speed and affine parameter.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the norm
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')$ is constant, so the causal character of $\gamma$
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant on $I$; a nonzero constant value
   makes $\gamma$ regular on all of $I$. If $\gamma$ is timelike and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then the proper-time
   increment of $\gamma$ over $[t_0,t]$ is $\lambda(t-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter of $\gamma$; the four-velocity
   $U=\lambda^{-1}\gamma'$ is parallel, $D_\tau U=0$ in the proper-time
   parameter. A null geodesic has $g(\gamma',\gamma')=0$ and admits no
   proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic and let
   $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto its open image with $h'\neq0$.
   Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and only if $h(s)=as+b$ with
   constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the constant
   $h'$, and every affine parameter of $\gamma$ arises in this way from a
   fixed one.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in I^-(p)\cap U$ and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their first
covariant derivatives along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development of the given data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $h$ be the auxiliary complete metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. Then for every $q\in M$ the
set
$$K_q:=J^-(q)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$$
is compact. Moreover $K_q=\{q\}$ when $q\in\Sigma$, and $K_q$ is empty when
$q\in I^-(\Sigma)$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

derivations.claim: (A boundary pair with a non-null-related second boundary point.) Choose $p_0\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$; since $\Sigma\subseteq U$ and $p_0\in\partial U$, one has $p_0\in I^+(\Sigma)$. If $J^-(p_0)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p_0\}$, the claim holds with $p:=p_0$. Otherwise choose $q_0\in J^-(p_0)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with $q_0\neq p_0$ and a future causal curve from $q_0$ to $p_0$. By achronality [L2] this curve has no timelike point and no corner, so by [L3] it is a null geodesic; extend it to the maximal geodesic $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=p_0$, $\gamma(1)=q_0$ and $\gamma$ past-inextendible at $\beta$.

(A point of $\gamma((0,1))$ cannot lie in $U$.) Suppose $\gamma(t_0)\in U$ for some $t_0\in(0,1)$ and let $(\alpha_0,\beta_0)\ni t_0$ be the maximal interval with $\gamma((\alpha_0,\beta_0))\subseteq U$. The restriction is a maximal geodesic of $U$, hence by [L4] inextendible in $U$ and therefore meets $\Sigma$ at a parameter $s\in(\alpha_0,\beta_0)$. Since $p_0=\gamma(0)$ and $q_0=\gamma(1)$ lie in $\partial U$ one has $\alpha_0\ge0$ and $\beta_0\le1$, so $s\in(0,1)$; also $\gamma(\alpha_0),\gamma(\beta_0)\in\partial U$ when these parameters lie in $(\alpha,\beta)$, and $\gamma(\beta_0)\le\gamma(s)\in\Sigma$, while $q_0=\gamma(1)\le\gamma(\beta_0)$ because $\beta_0\le1$, so $\gamma(\beta_0)\in J^+(\Sigma)\cap J^-(\Sigma)=\Sigma$ by [L1], contradicting $\gamma(\beta_0)\in\partial U$. Hence $\gamma((0,1))\cap U=\varnothing$.

(A point of $\gamma((0,1))$ cannot lie in the interior of the complement.) First a general exclusion, which is the content of the source's phrase that $r$ "could be connected by a timelike curve to $p$": **no point $r\in U^c\setminus\partial U$ with $r\in J^+(\Sigma)$ satisfies $r\le p$.** Indeed, since $U^c\setminus\partial U$ is open and $\gamma(t_1)\in U^c\setminus\partial U$ with $\gamma(t_1)\le\gamma(0)=p_0$, one finds $r\in U^c\setminus\partial U$ with $r\ll p_0$ (a small past timelike perturbation inside the open complement, using push-up [L3]); since $I^+(r)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is an open neighbourhood of $p_0$ and every neighbourhood of $p_0$ meets $U$, there is $s\in U\cap I^+(r)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Now choose a causal curve from $\Sigma$ to $r$ (possible since $r\in J^+(\Sigma)\setminus\Sigma=I^+(\Sigma)$, [L1]) and concatenate it with a timelike curve from $r$ to $s$: the result is a causal curve in $M$ from $\Sigma$ to the point $s\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ which passes through $r\notin U$, contradicting the convexity of [[lem-gr-subdevelopment-convexity]] clause (a) [L2]. Applying this exclusion with $r:=\gamma(t_1)$ and $p:=p_0$ contradicts the existence of $t_1$. Hence $\gamma((0,1))\cap(U^c\setminus\partial U)=\varnothing$.

(The boundary interval.) By steps 2.1 and 3.1, $\gamma((0,1))\subseteq\partial U$; by closedness of $\partial U$ also $\gamma(1)=q_0\in\partial U$ and $\gamma(0)=p_0\in\partial U$. Let $[0,b]:=\gamma^{-1}[\partial U]\cap[0,\beta)$; it is a closed interval containing $[0,1]$, and the same argument as in steps 2.1 and 3.1, applied to an arbitrary $t\in(0,b)$, shows $[0,b]\subseteq\partial U$ with $b<\beta$: if $\gamma([0,\beta))\subseteq\partial U$, then since $\gamma$ is a maximal geodesic of $M$ it meets $\Sigma$ exactly once by [L4], at a parameter $t_*\in(\alpha,\beta)$; but $\Sigma\subseteq U$ while $\gamma([0,\beta))\subseteq\partial U$ misses $U$ for parameters in $[0,\beta)$, and for the remaining parameters the unique crossing is on the future extension, say $t_*<0$; then $p_0=\gamma(0)\le\gamma(t_*)\in\Sigma$ gives $p_0\in J^-(\Sigma)$, and $p_0\in J^+(\Sigma)$ by construction, so $p_0\in\Sigma$ by [L1], contradicting $p_0\in\partial U$. Hence $b<\beta$, $\gamma(b)\in\partial U$, and $b$ is the last boundary parameter before $\Sigma$.

($\gamma(b)\in C$.) Let $J:=\{t\in[0,b]:\gamma(t)\in C\}$. By step 4.1 the segment $\gamma([0,b])$ lies in $\partial U$, and by clause (a) of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] ($C$ is open in $\partial U$) the set $J$ is open in $[0,b]$; $J$ is nonempty because $\gamma(0)=p_0\in C$. For closedness, let $t_j\in J$ with $t_j	o t_\infty\in[0,b]$. Since $\gamma([0,b])\subseteq\partial U$ and $J$ consists of $C$-points, the restriction $\gamma|_{J}$ is a null geodesic segment of $M$ whose image lies in $U\cup C$, so by [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] clause (d) the curve $t\mapsto\Phi(\gamma(t))$, $t\in J$, is a null geodesic in $M'$; write $\gamma'(t_j):=\Phi(\gamma(t_j))=\varphi(\gamma(t_j))$ for $t_j\in J$. ($J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}$ for $p:=\gamma(b)$.) Let $p:=\gamma(b)\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ (it lies in $J^+(\Sigma)$ since it is a causal point on the segment from $q_0\in J^+(\Sigma)$ forward, by [L1]). Suppose there were $q\in(J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma))\setminus\{p\}$. By the argument of step 1.1 the causal segment from $q$ to $p$ is a null geodesic contained in $\partial U$; concatenating it with $\gamma$ gives a broken null path from $q$ to $p$ through $\gamma(b)=p$ with a genuine corner at $p$ unless it is a continuation of the same geodesic. derivations.claim: (Setup.) Let $\gamma:[0,\varepsilon]\to M$ be a future timelike curve with $\gamma(0)=p$ (it exists since every point of a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold has a future timelike curve). If the conclusion failed for every $q=\gamma(t)$, there would be a sequence $t_j\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_j\to0$ and points $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(t_j))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$.

(Exclusion of $U^c\setminus\partial U$ points below $p$.) We show: there is no $r\in U^c\setminus\partial U$ with $r\le p$ and $r\in J^+(\Sigma)$. *First case: $r\ll p$.* Because $r\in U^c\setminus\partial U=\operatorname{int}(U^c)$ is interior to the complement and $I^+(r)$ is an open neighbourhood of $p\in\partial U$, the open set $I^+(r)$ meets $U$; choose $s\in I^+(r)\cap U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ (possible because $r\in J^+(\Sigma)\setminus\Sigma=I^+(\Sigma)$ and $I^+(r)$ is open, [L1]). Choose a causal curve $\alpha$ from $\Sigma$ to $r$ (exists as $r\in I^+(\Sigma)$) and a timelike curve from $r$ to $s$; their concatenation is a causal curve from $\Sigma$ to $s\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ whose image contains $r\notin U$, contradicting [L4] clause (a). *Second case: $r\le p$ but not $r\ll p$.* Then $r<p$, and any causal curve from $r$ to $p$ has no timelike point and no corner (otherwise its endpoints would be chronologically related, by the achronality argument recorded in the Facts of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]); in particular $p\in\partial I^-(r)$ and the null geodesic segment from $r$ to $p$ is unique up to parametrization. Since $r\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)$ is interior to the complement, there exist points $r_n\in I^+(r)\cap U^c\setminus\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ with $r_n\to r$ (small future timelike perturbations of $r$ inside the open sets $\operatorname{int}(U^c)$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$, [L1]); then $r_n\ll p$ by push-up, and the first case applied to $r_n$ gives a contradiction for every $n$. Hence no such $r$ exists.

(Compactness and a limit.) Fix any $t_\ast\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_\ast\ge t_j$ for all $j$ (equivalently pass to the subsequence with $t_j\le\varepsilon$); then $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$ for all $j$. Since $U^c$ and $W^c$ are closed and $J^+(\Sigma)$ is closed [L1], the set $J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$ is closed in the compact set $J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ of [L2], hence compact; passing to a subsequence, $q_j\to q$ with $q\in J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$.
($q\le p$.) Since $q_j\le\gamma(t_j)$ for every $j$, $q_j\to q$ and $\gamma(t_j)\to p$, closedness of the causal relation [L1] gives $q\le p$.

($q=p$, hence $q\in W$, contradiction.) If $q\in\partial U$, then $q\in J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}$ by the exposed-point property, so $q=p\in W$, contradicting $q\in W^c$ of step 2.2. Hence $q\in U^c\setminus\partial U$; but $q\le p$ by step 3.1 and $q\in J^+(\Sigma)$ by step 2.2, contradicting step 2.1. Therefore the assumption of step 1.1 is false: for every sufficiently small $t$ one has $J^-(\gamma(t))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W$, which is the assertion with $q:=\gamma(t)$.
