citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $h$ be the auxiliary
metric of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], so that
$(M,d_h)$ is complete and closed $d_h$-bounded sets are compact. Let
$$\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M,\qquad 0<b_k<\infty,$$
be future causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]])
parametrized by $h$-arclength, $\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for
$0\le s\le t\le b_k$, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x\in M$ and
$\alpha_k(b_k)\to z\in M$. Passing to a subsequence, let
$b:=\lim_kb_k\in[0,\infty]$. Then:

**(i) Bounded case.** If $b<\infty$, there is a subsequence and a future causal
curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$. If $b=0$ then $x=z$ and
$\alpha$ is the constant curve at $x$.

**(ii) Unbounded case.** If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future
causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are parameters $u_k\le v_k$ with
$u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$; in particular
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the closure of the causal relation in
the strong sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c):
there exist sequences $u_j\le v_j$ with $u_j\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and
$v_j\to\alpha^-(t_-)$.

**(iii) Coincident endpoints.** If $x=z$, then in case (i) with $b>0$ the
curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

**(iv) Imprisonment.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be strongly causal
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and
suppose all images $\alpha_k([0,b_k])$ are contained in one compact set $K$.
Then $b\le L(K)<\infty$ where $L(K)$ is the length bound of
[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $L_g$ be the Lorentzian
length functional of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] on future
causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). For a strictly
convex normal ball $U$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in U$ put
$$d_U(p,q):=\sqrt{\max\bigl(0,-g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))\bigr)},$$
a continuous function of $(p,q)$ on $U\times U$
([[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c)).

**(a) Refined sums.** Let $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ be a future causal curve and
let $(\mathcal P_N)$ be a sequence of partitions
$a=t_0^N<t_1^N<\dots<t_{m_N}^N=b$ with mesh tending to zero such that every
subarc $\alpha([t_i^N,t_{i+1}^N])$ is contained in a strictly convex normal
ball $U_i^N$ (such partitions exist and may be obtained from any fixed finite
cover of $\alpha([a,b])$ by strictly convex normal balls and a Lebesgue-number
subdivision). Then
$$L_g(\alpha)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{i=0}^{m_N-1}d_{U_i^N}\bigl(\alpha(t_i^N),\alpha(t_{i+1}^N)\bigr).$$
In particular the limit is independent of the choice of the partitions and of
the balls $U_i^N$.

**(b) Upper semicontinuity.** Let $\alpha_k:[a,b]\to M$ be future causal
curves converging to $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ uniformly on $[a,b]$ (in the manifold
topology, equivalently along any Riemannian distance). Then
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}L_g(\alpha_k)\le L_g(\alpha).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $p\in M$ and let $C$ be a
strictly convex normal coordinate ball around $p$ as produced by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], small enough that the exponential
chart
$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:C\to\mathbb R^4$$
of [[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
(for a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0$ future directed) satisfies
$$g(\nabla u^0,\nabla u^0)<0,\qquad g(\nabla u^0,N)>0\qquad\text{on }C;$$
such a choice exists because both inequalities hold at $p$ (where
$\nabla u^0=-\partial_0$) and are open conditions. Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$ and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))=\eta(u(q),u(q))$ on $C$, and let $J^+_C(p)$,
$I^+_C(p)$ be the sets of endpoints in $C$ of future causal, respectively
future timelike, curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with
image in $C$ starting at $p$. Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$ and every $t\in[0,1]$: the position
vector $v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero; equivalently
$D_p^2(\sigma(t))\le0$ and $u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.** With $\mathcal C^+$, $\mathcal T^+$,
$\mathcal N^+$ the sets of future causal or zero, future timelike, and
future null nonzero vectors of $\exp_p^{-1}(C)$ respectively,
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $p\in M$ and let
$U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$ be a normal neighborhood of $p$ as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Let
$\sigma:[a,b]\to U_p$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (locally absolutely continuous,
with future causal nonzero velocity almost everywhere), and write
$$v(t):=\exp_p^{-1}\bigl(\sigma(t)\bigr),\qquad P(t):=d(\exp_p)_{v(t)}(v(t)),\qquad Q(t):=g_p(v(t),v(t))$$
for $t\in[a,b]$. Suppose there is $t^*\in[a,b]$ such that $v(t^*)$ is
future timelike. Then:

**(a) Propagation.** For every $t\in[t^*,b]$ with
$\sigma([t^*,t])\subseteq U_p$, the vector $v(t)$ is future timelike;
consequently $Q(t)<0$, and $R(t):=\sqrt{-Q(t)}>0$.

**(b) Length inequality.** For all $t^*\le t_1<t_2\le b$ with
$\sigma([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U_p$,
$$R(t_2)-R(t_1)\ \ge\ L_g\bigl(\sigma|_{[t_1,t_2]}\bigr),$$
the Lorentzian length of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]].
In particular $R$ is nondecreasing on $[t^*,b]$.

**(c) Derivative formula.** The map $t\mapsto Q(t)$ is absolutely
continuous and
$$\frac{d}{dt}Q(t)=2\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(P(t),\sigma'(t)\bigr)$$
at almost every $t\in[a,b]$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let $\exp_q:\mathcal E_q\to M$
be the exponential maps of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. For an open set
$U\subseteq M$ write $T U\subseteq TM$ for the tangent vectors based at
points of $U$.

**(a) Normal neighborhood.** An open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M$ is a
**normal neighborhood of $p$** when there is an open star-shaped subset
$W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ of $T_pM$ such that $U=\exp_p(W)$ and
$\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
supplies such pairs). The **exponential coordinates at $p$** on such a $U$
are $u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$ for a linear isomorphism
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$.

**(b) Convex normal and strictly convex normal sets.** An open set
$C\subseteq M$ is **convex normal** when it is a normal neighborhood of each
of its points; thus for every $q\in C$ there is an open star-shaped
$C_q\subseteq\mathcal E_q$ with $\exp_q(C_q)=C$ and
$\exp_q|_{C_q}$ a diffeomorphism onto $C$. It is **strictly convex normal**
when in addition any two points of its closure $\overline C$ are joined by a
unique geodesic whose image is contained in $C$ except for the endpoints.

**(c) Position vector.** Let $C$ be convex normal, let $p,q\in C$ and let
$x:[0,1]\to C$ be the unique geodesic with $x(0)=p$, $x(1)=q$ supplied by
the definition of strict convexity outside the endpoints; equivalently
$x(t)=\exp_p(t\,\exp_p^{-1}(q))$ for $t\in[0,1]$ and
$v:=\exp_p^{-1}(q)\in T_pM$. The vector
$$P(p,q):=\gamma_{p,v}'(1)=d(\exp_p)_{v}(v)\in T_qM$$
is the **position vector of $q$ with respect to $p$**; here
$\gamma_{p,v}$ is the maximal geodesic of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. By the Gauss lemma of
[[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
$g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))$.

**(d) Squared-displacement function.** For a normal neighborhood $U$ of
$p$ the **squared-displacement function** is
$$D_p^2:U\to\mathbb R,\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p\bigl(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q)\bigr).$$
It is smooth on $U$ because $\exp_p^{-1}$ is smooth and $g_p$ is bilinear;
$D_p^2(p)=0$, $D_p^2(q)<0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is timelike,
$D_p^2(q)=0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is null or zero, and $D_p^2(q)>0$
exactly when $P(p,q)$ is spacelike. On a convex normal $C$ we write
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$, $D^2(p,q):=D_p^2(q)$, whenever the position
vector is defined.

**(e) Scope.** These are definitions inside the smooth Lorentzian model;
they assert no existence of convex normal sets (supplied separately by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), no completeness and no physical
reading. The position vector is an element of $T_qM$, not a vector field and
not a coordinate displacement; $D^2$ is not a metric distance and takes
negative values on timelike-separated pairs.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $L_g$ be the Lorentzian
length functional of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] on future
causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). For a strictly
convex normal ball $U$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in U$ put
$$d_U(p,q):=\sqrt{\max\bigl(0,-g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))\bigr)},$$
a continuous function of $(p,q)$ on $U\times U$
([[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c)).

**(a) Refined sums.** Let $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ be a future causal curve and
let $(\mathcal P_N)$ be a sequence of partitions
$a=t_0^N<t_1^N<\dots<t_{m_N}^N=b$ with mesh tending to zero such that every
subarc $\alpha([t_i^N,t_{i+1}^N])$ is contained in a strictly convex normal
ball $U_i^N$ (such partitions exist and may be obtained from any fixed finite
cover of $\alpha([a,b])$ by strictly convex normal balls and a Lebesgue-number
subdivision). Then
$$L_g(\alpha)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{i=0}^{m_N-1}d_{U_i^N}\bigl(\alpha(t_i^N),\alpha(t_{i+1}^N)\bigr).$$
In particular the limit is independent of the choice of the partitions and of
the balls $U_i^N$.

**(b) Upper semicontinuity.** Let $\alpha_k:[a,b]\to M$ be future causal
curves converging to $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ uniformly on $[a,b]$ (in the manifold
topology, equivalently along any Riemannian distance). Then
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}L_g(\alpha_k)\le L_g(\alpha).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $p\in M$ and let $C$ be a
strictly convex normal coordinate ball around $p$ as produced by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], small enough that the exponential
chart
$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:C\to\mathbb R^4$$
of [[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
(for a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0$ future directed) satisfies
$$g(\nabla u^0,\nabla u^0)<0,\qquad g(\nabla u^0,N)>0\qquad\text{on }C;$$
such a choice exists because both inequalities hold at $p$ (where
$\nabla u^0=-\partial_0$) and are open conditions. Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$ and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))=\eta(u(q),u(q))$ on $C$, and let $J^+_C(p)$,
$I^+_C(p)$ be the sets of endpoints in $C$ of future causal, respectively
future timelike, curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with
image in $C$ starting at $p$. Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$ and every $t\in[0,1]$: the position
vector $v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero; equivalently
$D_p^2(\sigma(t))\le0$ and $u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.** With $\mathcal C^+$, $\mathcal T^+$,
$\mathcal N^+$ the sets of future causal or zero, future timelike, and
future null nonzero vectors of $\exp_p^{-1}(C)$ respectively,
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.

3. **Geodesic speed and affine parameter.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the norm
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')$ is constant, so the causal character of $\gamma$
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant on $I$; a nonzero constant value
   makes $\gamma$ regular on all of $I$. If $\gamma$ is timelike and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then the proper-time
   increment of $\gamma$ over $[t_0,t]$ is $\lambda(t-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter of $\gamma$; the four-velocity
   $U=\lambda^{-1}\gamma'$ is parallel, $D_\tau U=0$ in the proper-time
   parameter. A null geodesic has $g(\gamma',\gamma')=0$ and admits no
   proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic and let
   $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto its open image with $h'\neq0$.
   Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and only if $h(s)=as+b$ with
   constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the constant
   $h'$, and every affine parameter of $\gamma$ arises in this way from a
   fixed one.

derivations.claim: (Finiteness.) Let $r\in J^-(q)$ and let $\alpha$ be any future causal curve from $r$ to $q$. Every point of $\alpha$ lies in $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$, which is compact, so by [L1] the $h$-arclength of $\alpha$ and hence $L_g(\alpha)$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,q$; therefore $\tau_q(r)<\infty$. If $r\notin J^-(q)$ no such curve exists and $\tau_q(r)=0$; if $r=q$ the constant curve gives $\tau_q(q)=0\le\tau_q(r)$; and $\tau_q(r)>0$ iff there is a future timelike curve from $r$ to $q$, i.e. $r\in I^-(q)$.

(Attainment and geodesy of maximizers.) Let $r\in J^-(q)$ and let $\alpha_n$ be causal curves from $r$ to $q$ with $L_g(\alpha_n)\to\tau_q(r)$. All images lie in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$; reparametrizing by $h$-arclength from $r$ and applying [L2] gives a subsequence converging uniformly to a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$, and upper semicontinuity of length [L2] gives $L_g(\gamma)\ge\limsup L_g(\alpha_n)=\tau_q(r)$, so $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. If $\gamma$ had a timelike point or a corner, replacing a small subsegment by the radial segment in a convex normal neighbourhood ([L3], [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]] (b)) would produce a causal curve from $r$ to $q$ of strictly larger length, contradicting maximality; hence every maximizer is a causal geodesic up to monotone reparametrization, and its image lies in $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$.

(The radial formula.) Let $V,W,q$ be as in clause (b) and let $r\in W\cap I^-(q)$. Let $\gamma$ be a maximizer from $r$ to $q$ (step 2.1). Since $W$ is causally convex, $\gamma\subseteq W\subseteq V$; by [L3] applied in $V$ with base point $q$, every causal curve in $V$ from $r$ to $q$ has length at most $\sqrt{-g_q(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r))}$, with equality exactly for the radial geodesic, which lies in $V$; since all competitors from $r$ to $q$ lie in $W\subseteq V$ and the radial segment itself is a competitor with that length, $\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r))}$. The right-hand side is smooth on $I^-(q)\cap W$ by [L3] and the smoothness of the inverse exponential map; its continuous extension by $0$ at points of $W\setminus J^-(q)$ and at $q$ is exactly $\tau_q$ there by step 1.1.

(Upper semicontinuity on compact sets.) Let $r_n\to r$ in a compact $K$ and let $\alpha_n$ be causal curves from $r_n$ to $q$ with $L_g(\alpha_n)\ge\tau_q(r_n)-1/n$. Passing to the compact diamond $J^+(K')\cap J^-(q)$ for a compact $K'$ containing the $r_n$ ([L1]), [L2] gives a subsequence of the $\alpha_n$, reparametrized by $h$-arclength, converging uniformly to a causal curve from $r$ to $q$, and $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\limsup_nL_g(\alpha_n)\le L_g(\gamma)\le\tau_q(r)$ by upper semicontinuity [L2] and step 2.1. If $r\in I^-(q)$ then a maximizer $\gamma_r$ from $r$ to $q$ exists (step 2.1); since $I^-(q)$ is open, for $n$ large the inner segment of $\gamma_r$ can be joined to $r_n$ by a short timelike segment inside $I^-(q)$, giving $\liminf_n\tau_q(r_n)\ge\tau_q(r)$ by letting the inner cut shrink; combined with the upper bound this gives continuity at $r$.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and definitions: every quantified object (manifolds, developments, hypersurfaces, curves, sets) is nonempty by hypothesis, a development contains the initial surface $j(\Sigma)$; no step forms an empty intersection, union or index range, and vacuous subcases are excluded by those nonemptiness hypotheses.

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.
Statement: the quantifiers range over all objects of the stated class, so the one-element and singleton instances are covered by the same argument; no step separates a cardinality-one case.

Statement: degeneracy is excluded by the standing hypotheses (nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, spacelike embedded hypersurface, embeddings with injective differential where used); no step proceeds through a degenerate configuration.

Statement and proof: the endpoint behaviour of the closed parameter intervals and of the boundary points of $U$ is handled explicitly where it occurs (limits of curves at the ends of their intervals, the closedness of $\partial U$); no completeness or extendibility beyond the stated domains is inferred.

Statement: the declared choice principles are used exactly for the stated countable selections (countable atlases, dense-set recursion); no other choice is invoked and no step needs a choice on an uncountable family.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$L_g$ be the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), and for $q\in M$ define the
**time separation**
$$\tau_q:M\to[0,\infty),\qquad \tau_q(r):=\sup\{L_g(\alpha):\ \alpha \text{ is a future causal curve from } r \text{ to } q\},$$
the supremum over the empty set being $0$; thus $\tau_q(r)>0$ exactly for
$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

**(a)** For every $r\in J^-(q)$ one has $0\le\tau_q(r)<\infty$, and the
supremum is attained: there is a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$
with $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. Every such **maximizer** is, up to monotone
reparametrization, a causal geodesic, and its image lies in the compact set
$J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$.

**(b)** Let $V$ be a strictly convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ (as produced
by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and let $W\subseteq V$ be open and
causally convex in $M$ (every causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $W$
is contained in $W$), with $\overline W$ compact and $q\in W$. Then for every
$r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q\bigl(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r)\bigr)},$$
so $\tau_q$ is smooth on $W\cap I^-(q)$ and extends continuously by
$\tau_q(q)=0$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\in W\setminus J^-(q)$.

**(c)** On every compact set $K\subseteq M$ the function $\tau_q$ is upper
semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in
$K$ one has $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\tau_q(r)$. If moreover $r\in I^-(q)$,
then $\tau_q(r_n)\to\tau_q(r)$ for every sequence $r_n\to r$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development of the given data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $h$ be the auxiliary complete metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. Then for every $q\in M$ the
set
$$K_q:=J^-(q)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$$
is compact. Moreover $K_q=\{q\}$ when $q\in\Sigma$, and $K_q$ is empty when
$q\in I^-(\Sigma)$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$L_g$ be the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), and for $q\in M$ define the
**time separation**
$$\tau_q:M\to[0,\infty),\qquad \tau_q(r):=\sup\{L_g(\alpha):\ \alpha \text{ is a future causal curve from } r \text{ to } q\},$$
the supremum over the empty set being $0$; thus $\tau_q(r)>0$ exactly for
$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

**(a)** For every $r\in J^-(q)$ one has $0\le\tau_q(r)<\infty$, and the
supremum is attained: there is a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$
with $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. Every such **maximizer** is, up to monotone
reparametrization, a causal geodesic, and its image lies in the compact set
$J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$.

**(b)** Let $V$ be a strictly convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ (as produced
by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and let $W\subseteq V$ be open and
causally convex in $M$ (every causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $W$
is contained in $W$), with $\overline W$ compact and $q\in W$. Then for every
$r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q\bigl(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r)\bigr)},$$
so $\tau_q$ is smooth on $W\cap I^-(q)$ and extends continuously by
$\tau_q(q)=0$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\in W\setminus J^-(q)$.

**(c)** On every compact set $K\subseteq M$ the function $\tau_q$ is upper
semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in
$K$ one has $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\tau_q(r)$. If moreover $r\in I^-(q)$,
then $\tau_q(r_n)\to\tau_q(r)$ for every sequence $r_n\to r$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), let $p\in M$ and let $U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$
be a normal neighborhood of $p$ with $W_p$ star-shaped, as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$ for $q\in U_p$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$, and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))$.

**(a) Differential in the second argument.** $D_p^2$ is smooth on $U_p$ and,
for every $q\in U_p$ and every $w\in T_qM$,
$$d(D_p^2)_q(w)=2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

**(b) Reversal.** Let $q\in U_p$ and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$,
$\gamma(t)=\exp_p(t\,v(q))$, be the radial geodesic, so that
$\gamma(1)=q$. Then the reversed curve $t\mapsto\gamma(1-t)$ is the maximal
geodesic from $q$ with initial velocity $-P(p,q)$; consequently
$$\exp_q^{-1}(p)=-P(p,q)\quad\text{and}\quad P(q,p)=-\,v(q)=-(\exp_p)^{-1}(q)$$
whenever both sides are defined, and then $D^2(q,p)=D^2(p,q)$ by the Gauss
lemma of [[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]].

**(c) Differential on pairs in a convex normal set.** If $C$ is a convex
normal set ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and $p,q\in C$, then
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$ is smooth and for all $u\in T_pM$, $w\in T_qM$,
$$dD^2(p,q)(u,w)=2\,g_p\bigl(P(q,p),u\bigr)+2\,g_q\bigl(P(p,q),w\bigr).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $p\in M$ and let $C$ be a
strictly convex normal coordinate ball around $p$ as produced by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], small enough that the exponential
chart
$$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:C\to\mathbb R^4$$
of [[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
(for a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0$ future directed) satisfies
$$g(\nabla u^0,\nabla u^0)<0,\qquad g(\nabla u^0,N)>0\qquad\text{on }C;$$
such a choice exists because both inequalities hold at $p$ (where
$\nabla u^0=-\partial_0$) and are open conditions. Write
$v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q)$, $P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q))$ and
$D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q))=\eta(u(q),u(q))$ on $C$, and let $J^+_C(p)$,
$I^+_C(p)$ be the sets of endpoints in $C$ of future causal, respectively
future timelike, curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with
image in $C$ starting at $p$. Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$ and every $t\in[0,1]$: the position
vector $v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero; equivalently
$D_p^2(\sigma(t))\le0$ and $u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.** With $\mathcal C^+$, $\mathcal T^+$,
$\mathcal N^+$ the sets of future causal or zero, future timelike, and
future null nonzero vectors of $\exp_p^{-1}(C)$ respectively,
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$ with maximal flow $\Phi$, and let
$S\hookrightarrow M$ be an embedded codimension-one submanifold. If $X_p\notin T_pS$
for every $p\in S$, then there is an open neighbourhood
$\mathcal O\subseteq \mathbb R\times S$ of $\{0\}\times S$ such that the map

$$ F:\mathcal O\to M,\qquad F(t,p)=\Phi_t(p), $$

is an embedding. Its image is a flowout of $S$ along $X$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be as in
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a): $M$ is
a development of the given data, $U\subseteq M$ is open with
$j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$, and $U$ with the restricted fields is again a
development of the same data. Write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and compute
$I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ and $\le$ in $M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Then:

**(a) Past convexity within the future of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in\Sigma$ and $\nu(b)\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$
one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(b) Future convexity within the past of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in U\cap I^-(\Sigma)$ and
$\nu(b)\in\Sigma$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(c) Segments with endpoints in $U$.** For every future causal curve
$\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a),\nu(b)\in U$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in I^-(p)\cap U$ and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their first
covariant derivatives along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

derivations.claim: (Attainment and the location of maximizers; clause (a).) $K$ is compact ([L2]), nonempty ($p\in K$, [L2]), and $\tau_q$ is upper semicontinuous on $K$ and finite there, so $\tau_0$ is attained ([L1]); $\tau_0\ge\tau_q(p)>0$ ([L2]). Let $r_0\in K$ be a maximizer. Then $\tau_q(r_0)=\tau_0>0$, so $r_0\in I^-(q)$; and $r_0\in J^+(\Sigma)\setminus\Sigma$ (as $\Sigma\subseteq U$ and $r_0\in U^c$), so $r_0\in I^+(\Sigma)$. Hence $r_0\in J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W$ by the choice of $q$, so $r_0\in W$. Suppose $r_0\in U^c\setminus\partial U$. Then $r_0\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)$ is an interior point of the complement and lies in the open set $W$. Let $\gamma$ be a maximizer from $r_0$ to $q$ and continue it a little to the past: for small $\varepsilon>0$ the point $r':=\gamma(-\varepsilon)$ lies in $W\cap\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)=W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ (all three sets open at $r_0$) and $$\tau_q(r')\ \ge\ L_g(\gamma|_{[-\varepsilon,1]})\ =\ \tau_0+L_g(\gamma|_{[-\varepsilon,0]})\ >\ \tau_0,$$ contradicting the maximality of $\tau_0$ on $K$. Hence every maximizer lies in $\partial U\cap W$, and since $W\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ ([L5]) in $W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$. If $x\in W$ satisfied $\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$, then $x\in I^-(q)$ and $x\in W\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$, so $x\in K$; if $x\notin U$ this contradicts the maximality of $\tau_0$, so $x\in U$. This proves all assertions of clause (a).

(The level set; clause (b).) On $W^\circ=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ the function $\tau_q$ is smooth with everywhere nonzero gradient ([L1], [L3]), so $Z:=\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ is a closed embedded $3$-submanifold of the open four-manifold $W^\circ$; its connected component $S$ is therefore an embedded submanifold of $W^\circ$ without boundary, hence of $M$, with timelike normal $\nabla\tau_q$ and thus spacelike. $S$ is nonempty because a maximizer $x_0$ of $\tau_q$ over $K$ satisfies $x_0\in W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and $\tau_q(x_0)=\tau_0$, so $x_0\in Z$. Since $S\subseteq Z\subseteq W^\circ\subseteq W$ and every point of $Z$ with $\tau_q(x)=\tau_0>0$ satisfies $x\in I^-(q)$, we get $S\subseteq W\cap(\overline U\cup\partial U)$: indeed if $x\in S\cap U^c$ then $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ ([L6]) with $\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$, so clause (a) gives $x\in\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; in particular $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$ since the maximizer $x_0$ lies in $S\cap\partial U$. This is clause (b).

(Finite length of the base curve, and at most one meeting with $S$.) Let $\gamma:I\to N$ be a causal curve and write it as $\gamma(t)=F(s(t),t_\gamma(t))$ with $t_\gamma=\tau_q\circ\gamma-\tau_0$. The curve $s(\cdot)$ is locally absolutely continuous and $$-t_\gamma'^2+q_{t_\gamma}(s')(s',s')\le0\quad\text{a.e.},$$ where $q_\tau$ is the induced metric on the level set $F(S\times\{\tau\})$ pulled back to $S$ ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]]). Since $\nabla_X X=0$ with $X$ smooth on a compact neighbourhood of $\overline N$, the flow derivatives satisfy $\|d\phi_t\|\le e^{C|t|}$ for $|t|\le\delta_0$ on $S$ ([L3]), so $q_\tau(s)\le e^{2C\delta_0}q_0(s)$ at every $s$; hence $$\int_I\sqrt{q_0(s')(s',s')}\,dt\ \le\ e^{2C\delta_0}\int_I|t_\gamma'|\,dt\ =\ e^{2C\delta_0}\cdot\operatorname{var}(t_\gamma)\ <\ \infty.$$ So $s(\cdot)$ has finite length in the fixed metric $q_0$. Since $\overline S\cap\overline W$ is compact and the intrinsic metric $q_0$ dominates the auxiliary metric $h$ there, $s(t)$ has a limit in $\overline S\cap\overline W$ whenever its parameter tends to an end of $I$ with $\operatorname{var}t_\gamma\to0$ near that end; in particular $s$ extends continuously to both ends of the interval and $\gamma$ converges in $M$ at an end whenever $t_\gamma$ does. Moreover $t_\gamma=\tau_q\circ\gamma-\tau_0$ is strictly monotone: on $\{\tau_q>0\}$ the $1$-form $d\tau_q$ has no nonzero causal kernel because $\nabla\tau_q$ is timelike, and it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]); hence its sign along the causal curve is constant and $t_\gamma$ is strictly monotone ([L1], [L3]). Consequently $\gamma$ meets $S$ (that is, $t_\gamma=0$) in at most one parameter value. This is clause (c)1.

(Every $U$-avoiding inextendible curve meets $S$; clause (c)2.) Let $\gamma:I\to U\cup N$ be a causal curve, inextendible in $U\cup N$ and with image disjoint from $U$. Then $\gamma\subseteq N\setminus U$ and $\gamma^{-1}(N)=I$; by [[lem-gr-portion-inextendibility]] applied with $V=N\subseteq U\cup N$, the curve $\gamma$ is inextendible in $N$. Write $\gamma(t)=F(s(t),t_\gamma(t))$ as in step 4.1. By clause (a), all points of $N$ with $t_\gamma>0$ (that is, $\tau_q>\tau_0$) lie in $U$; since $\gamma$ avoids $U$, $t_\gamma(t)<0$ for all $t$. Being strictly monotone, $t_\gamma$ is decreasing (the future-directed case; the past-directed case is the time reversal); let $L:=\lim_{t\to\sup I}t_\gamma$ and $H:=\lim_{t\to\inf I}t_\gamma$, with $-\delta_0<L\le H\le0$.

(End types.) Consider the past end $t\to\inf I$. By step 4.1, $s(t)$ converges in $\overline S\cap\overline W$ to a point $e$; write $e\in S$ or $e\in\overline S\setminus S$. Since $F$ is obtained from a smooth flow and $\operatorname{dist}_h(F(s,t),s)\le c_0|t|$, the curves $\gamma(t)$ converge in $M$ to the point $F(e,H)$ (where $F$ is extended by limits along flow lines) whenever $|H|<\delta(e)$; and $H\ge-\liminf_{t\to\inf I}\delta(s(t))\ge-\delta(e)$. Thus exactly one of the following holds at the past end: (i) $e\in S$ and $H>-\delta(e)$: then $\gamma(t)\to F(e,H)\in N$, contradicting inextendibility of $\gamma$ in $N$; (ii) $e\in S$ and $H=-\delta(e)$: the past end lies on the "past face" of the tube; then $H=\tau_q-\tau_0=-\delta(e)<0$ and $t_\gamma\le H<0$ on all of $I$; (iii) $e\in\overline S\setminus S$: then $\operatorname{dist}_h(s(t),M\setminus W)\to0$, so $\delta(s(t))\to0$ by the choice of $\delta$, and therefore $H=0$ and $\gamma(t)\to e$; since $e\in\partial W\cap\{\tau_q=\tau_0\}$ and any point of $\partial W$ with $\tau_q=\tau_0$ lies in $U$ (otherwise it would belong to $K$ and to $J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W$, contradicting $e\in\partial W$), we get $e\in U\subseteq U\cup N$, so $\gamma$ converges to a point of $U\cup N$ at the past end, contradicting inextendibility in $U\cup N$. The same analysis applies at the future end, with limits $L$ and $e'\in\overline S$; the analogue of (iii) again contradicts inextendibility in $U\cup N$.

(Exclusion of the remaining cases.) Suppose case (ii) occurs at the past end and let $e'\in\overline S$ be the limit of $s(t)$ at the future end. Case (iii) at the future end is excluded by step 6.1; case (i) at the future end is excluded because $\gamma$ is inextendible in $N$; so the future end is again of type (ii): $e'\in S$, $L=-\delta(e')$. Set $\eta(t):=t_\gamma(t)+\delta(s(t))$ (the "signed distance to the past face"). Along $\gamma$, $$\eta'(t)=t_\gamma'(t)+\frac{d}{dt}\delta(s(t))\ \le\ t_\gamma'(t)+\ell\,\sqrt{q_{t_\gamma}(s')(s',s')}\ \le\ t_\gamma'(t)+\ell\,|t_\gamma'(t)|\ =\ (\ell-1)\,|t_\gamma'(t)|\ <\ 0$$ almost everywhere, where $\ell<1$ is the Lipschitz constant of $\delta$ with respect to the metrics $q_\tau$ (achieved by the choice of $\varepsilon$), and we used causality and $t_\gamma'<0$. If (ii) holds at both ends, then $\eta\ge0$ on $I$ while $\eta\to0$ at both ends and $\eta$ is strictly decreasing, which is impossible. Hence (ii) cannot occur at the past end either. Similarly (with $\psi(t):=\delta(s(t))-t_\gamma(t)$ for the future face) the future face cannot be an end. Therefore every end of $\gamma$ is of type (i) or (iii), both of which are impossible; hence no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ can avoid $U$.

(Restatement; clause (c)2.) Combining the preceding steps: every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets $U$. Applying [[lem-gr-portion-inextendibility]] with $V=U\subseteq U\cup N$, each component of the preimage of $U$ is inextendible in $U$ and therefore meets $\Sigma$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)5); so every such curve meets $\Sigma$ at least once. It meets $\Sigma$ at most once: if $\gamma(t_1),\gamma(t_2)\in\Sigma$ with $t_1<t_2$, the subsegment $\gamma|_{[t_1,t_2]}$ is a causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $U$ (as $\Sigma\subseteq U$), hence is contained in $U$ by [[lem-gr-subdevelopment-convexity]] clause (c) ([L4]), and its endpoints are causally related points of the Cauchy set $\Sigma$ of the development $U$, which are equal or fail the Cauchy property of $\Sigma$ in $U$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c), [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)5). This is clause (c)2.

(The radial segment lies in $U$; clause (c)3.) Let $y\in N\cap U$ and write $y=F(s,t_y)$ with $s\in S$ and $|t_y|<\delta(s)$. The radial segment $\Sigma_y:=\{F(s,u):u	ext{ between }0	ext{ and }t_y\}$ is contained in $N$ and hence in $W$ by step 3.1, so $\Sigma_y\subseteq W\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ ([L6]); it is a geodesic segment, and $F(s,u)$ is timelike for every $u
e0$ ([L3]). Suppose that some $z=F(s,u_z)$ with $u_z
e0$ lay outside $U$. Since $z\in W\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$, there is a future timelike curve $ eta$ from a point of $\Sigma$ to $z$ ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c)). If $u_z
e t_y$, then the subsegment of $\Sigma_y$ from $z$ to $y$ is a nondegenerate timelike geodesic segment, and its concatenation with $ eta$ is a future causal curve from $\Sigma$ to $y$ passing through $z
otin U$; since $y\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$, this contradicts the past convexity of the subdevelopment, [[lem-gr-subdevelopment-convexity]] clause (a) ([L4]). If $u_z=t_y$, then $z=y\in U$, contrary to the assumption. Hence no such $z$ exists, that is, $\Sigma_y\setminus\{s\}\subseteq U$. This is clause (c)3.

boundaries.evidence: Statement and definitions: every quantified object (manifolds, developments, hypersurfaces, curves, sets) is nonempty by hypothesis, a development contains the initial surface $j(\Sigma)$; no step forms an empty intersection, union or index range, and vacuous subcases are excluded by those nonemptiness hypotheses.

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.
Statement: the quantifiers range over all objects of the stated class, so the one-element and singleton instances are covered by the same argument; no step separates a cardinality-one case.

Statement: degeneracy is excluded by the standing hypotheses (nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, spacelike embedded hypersurface, embeddings with injective differential where used); no step proceeds through a degenerate configuration.

Statement and proof: the endpoint behaviour of the closed parameter intervals and of the boundary points of $U$ is handled explicitly where it occurs (limits of curves at the ends of their intervals, the closedness of $\partial U$); no completeness or extendibility beyond the stated domains is inferred.

Statement: the declared choice principles are used exactly for the stated countable selections (countable atlases, dense-set recursion); no other choice is invoked and no step needs a choice on an uncountable family.
