citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
Call a map $x:I\to M$ a **geodesically connectible continuous causal curve**
when it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and for every strictly convex
normal ball $C$ as produced by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]
([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b)) and all
$t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $x([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$, the endpoints $x(t_1)$ and
$x(t_2)$ are joined by a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in
$C$. Write $\le$ for the causal relation of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (defined by locally absolutely
continuous future causal curves) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat .$$

**(a) Absolutely continuous implies connectible.** Every future causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve.

**(b) Connectible curves give causal relations.** Let $x:I\to M$ be a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve and let $t_1<t_2$ in $I$.
Then for every open neighborhood $W$ of $x([t_1,t_2])$ there is a piecewise
smooth future causal curve $\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with $\eta(t_1)=x(t_1)$ and
$\eta(t_2)=x(t_2)$ (in particular a locally absolutely continuous future
causal curve, so $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$ in the relation defined by
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

**(c) Equality of relations.** For $p,q\in M$ the following are equivalent:
$p\le q$; $p=q$ or there is a geodesically connectible continuous causal
curve with endpoints $p,q$.

**(d) One-sided extension.** Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a
future-inextendible future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). Then there is an
inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^*:I^*\to M$ with
$[0,\infty)\subseteq I^*\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\gamma^*|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$;
that is, $\gamma$ is contained in a curve that is both future- and
past-inextendible. The dual statement holds for past-inextendible curves.

No choice principle is used. The extension in (d) is not asserted to be
unique.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field with its order and
absolute value ([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]), and
neighbourhoods are those of [[def-neighbourhood-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$. Then
$f$ is **continuous at $c$** when

$$(\forall \varepsilon > 0)\ (\exists \delta > 0)\ (\forall x \in A)\ \bigl[\ |x - c| < \delta \ \Longrightarrow\ |f(x) - f(c)| < \varepsilon\ \bigr],$$

with $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ ranging over the **positive reals**. In the
language of neighbourhoods: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ with

$$f\bigl(A \cap N_{\delta}(c)\bigr) \;\subseteq\; N_{\varepsilon}\bigl(f(c)\bigr).$$

$f$ is **continuous on $A$** when it is continuous at every point of $A$.

**The point $c$ is required to lie in $A$, and the condition is unpunctured.**
Both differ from [[def-function-limit]], and deliberately. There the quantifier
runs over $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, which removes $x = c$; here $x = c$ is allowed,
and at $x = c$ the implication reads $|f(c) - f(c)| = 0 < \varepsilon$, which is
automatic. So allowing $x = c$ costs nothing, and it is what lets the definition
be stated at every point of $A$, including the points where no limit exists.

**Three clauses, and all three are part of the definition.**

1. **At a limit point.** Suppose $c \in A$ is a limit point of $A$
   ([[def-limit-point-r]]). Then $f$ is continuous at $c$ if and only if the
   limit of $f$ at $c$ exists and
   $$\lim_{x \to c} f(x) \;=\; f(c)$$
   ([[def-function-limit]]). Indeed, for a given $\varepsilon > 0$ a $\delta$
   witnessing continuity witnesses the limit condition, because the limit
   condition quantifies over a subset of the points continuity quantifies over;
   and conversely a $\delta$ witnessing $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ witnesses
   continuity, because the one point it omits, $x = c$, satisfies
   $|f(c) - f(c)| < \varepsilon$ anyway.

2. **At an isolated point.** Suppose $c \in A$ is an isolated point of $A$
   ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so that $N_{\eta}(c) \cap A = \{c\}$ for some real
   $\eta > 0$. Then **every** $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous at $c$: take
   $\delta := \eta$, so that the only $x \in A$ with $|x - c| < \delta$ is $c$
   itself, and $|f(c) - f(c)| = 0 < \varepsilon$.

3. **On a set.** Continuity on $A$ is continuity at each point of $A$, and
   nothing more. It is not a condition relating $f$ to points outside $A$.

Every point of $A$ is either a limit point of $A$ or an isolated point of $A$,
and never both ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so clauses 1 and 2 between them describe
continuity at every point of $A$.

**This is not the raw $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula of
[[fs-limit-unique-at-every-point-of-the-domain]].** That item records what goes
wrong when the *punctured* formula of [[def-function-limit]] is written down at
an arbitrary point of the domain: at an isolated point it is satisfied
vacuously by every real $L$ at once, so it defines nothing, and this library
therefore leaves $\lim_{x \to c} f(x)$ **undefined** at an isolated point.
Continuity at an isolated point is a different matter: the formula above is not
vacuous — it is a genuine condition on $f(c)$, satisfied because $f(c)$ is the
only value being compared with itself — and it names a single, well-defined
property. The limit is undefined there; the continuity is defined, and is
automatic. Clause 1 is the only place where the two notions meet, and it is
stated only where the limit exists as a notion.

**Where the distinction disappears.** If $A$ is an open subset of $\mathbb{R}$
([[def-open-and-closed-in-r]]), then every $c \in A$ has some
$N_{\eta}(c) \subseteq A$, and a punctured neighbourhood is never empty
([[def-neighbourhood-r]]), so every point of $A$ is a limit point of $A$ and
clause 1 covers the whole of $A$. The same holds when $A$ is a nondegenerate
interval ([[def-interval]]). Isolated points are what force clause 2 to exist at
all, and they occur as soon as $A$ is allowed to be an arbitrary subset of
$\mathbb{R}$, as in $A = \{0\} \cup [1,2]$.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-ordered-field]]) with its order
([[def-real-order]]).

A subset $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is **order-convex** when

$$x, y \in I \text{ and } x \le z \le y \;\Longrightarrow\; z \in I .$$

The **intervals** of $\mathbb{R}$ are the sets of the following nine forms, where
$a, b \in \mathbb{R}$:

| | bounded forms | | one-sided and full forms |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(a,b)$ | $\{x : a < x < b\}$ | $(a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a < x\}$ |
| $[a,b]$ | $\{x : a \le x \le b\}$ | $[a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a \le x\}$ |
| $[a,b)$ | $\{x : a \le x < b\}$ | $(-\infty,b)$ | $\{x : x < b\}$ |
| $(a,b]$ | $\{x : a < x \le b\}$ | $(-\infty,b]$ | $\{x : x \le b\}$ |
| | | $(-\infty,\infty)$ | $\mathbb{R}$ |

An interval is **open** when both of its written endpoints are excluded, that is
for the forms $(a,b)$, $(a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b)$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$; it is
**closed** when both written endpoints are included, that is for $[a,b]$,
$[a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b]$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$. The forms $[a,b)$ and
$(a,b]$ are **half-open**.

**The symbols $\pm\infty$ are notation and not elements of $\mathbb{R}$.** They
mark which side carries no endpoint condition at all; the five forms in the right
column are defined by the displayed conditions on $x$ alone, and no arithmetic is
ever performed with $\infty$. This is the same refusal to extend $\mathbb{R}$
silently that [[rem-sup-conventions]] records for suprema.

**Every one of the nine forms is order-convex.** Each is defined by a conjunction
of at most two conditions, each of the shape $a < x$, $a \le x$, $x < b$ or
$x \le b$, and each such condition is inherited by an intermediate point: if
$a < x$ and $x \le z$ then $a < z$, and if $z \le y$ and $y < b$ then $z < b$,
by transitivity of the order ([[def-ordered-field]]). Applying this to whichever
one or two conditions define the form in question gives $z \in I$ whenever
$x, y \in I$ and $x \le z \le y$.

**Bounded intervals.** An interval is **bounded** ([[def-bounded-set]]) exactly
when it is of one of the four forms in the left column: for those, $a$ is a lower
bound and $b$ an upper bound. The other five forms are unbounded, on the side or
sides written with $\infty$; the verification is in the remarks below.

**Nondegeneracy.** An interval is **degenerate** when it has at most one element,
and **nondegenerate** when it has at least two. For the four bounded forms with
endpoints $a$ and $b$:

- $[a,b]$ is nonempty exactly when $a \le b$, and it is nondegenerate exactly
  when $a < b$. It is the singleton $\{a\}$ when $a = b$.
- $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are nonempty exactly when $a < b$, and then each
  is nondegenerate.

The only assertion here that is not immediate from the defining conditions is
that $a < b$ makes $(a,b)$ nonempty with at least two points. It holds because
$a < (a+b)/2 < b$, which follows from $a < b$ by adding $a$, respectively $b$, to
both sides and halving ([[def-ordered-field]]); repeating the halving inside
$(a, (a+b)/2)$ produces a second point.

**Closed bounded intervals.** These are the sets $[a,b]$ with $a \le b$, which is
exactly the condition making them nonempty. They are the intervals the nested
interval property is stated for, and the phrase *closed bounded interval* always
carries the hypothesis $a \le b$ in this library.

**Length.** The **length** of a bounded interval presented by its endpoints
$a \le b$ is

$$\ell = b - a \;\ge\; 0 .$$

Length is attached to the presentation by endpoints and is not recovered from the
set: $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are all empty when $a = b$, and so is
$(c,c)$ for any other $c$, while each of these presentations has length $0$, so
nothing inconsistent arises; but the endpoints are named explicitly at every
point where a length is used in this library, and never inferred from the set.
Unbounded intervals are assigned no length.

derivations.claim: (External structural facts, quoted.) The following published statements about causal and timelike curves as in [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] are used. (i) *Equality of the causal and timelike domains for closed $S$.* [Minguzzi, Section 3: "Let $S$ be a closed set then $D^+(S)=\widetilde D^+(S)$, $\operatorname{Int}\widetilde D^+(S)=\operatorname{Int}D^+(S)$ and $\dot{\widetilde D^+}(S)=\dot D^+(S)$", the proof establishing that $\widetilde D^+(S)$ is closed; and the achronality identity "If $S$ is achronal, $\widetilde D^+(S)\cap\widetilde D^-(S)=D^+(S)\cap D^-(S)=S$".] (ii) *Openness for partial Cauchy hypersurfaces.* [Minguzzi, Section 3: "Let $S$ be a partial Cauchy hypersurface, then $D(S)\cap H(S)=\varnothing$, in particular $D(S)$ is open and $H^\pm(S)\subset I^\pm(S)$".] Here $H(S)$ is the Cauchy horizon of $S$, the part of the boundary of the domain of dependence other than $S$; since $D(S)$ is closed ([L1] with [L1]'s equality for the closed set $S$), its boundary contains no point of $D(S)\setminus S$ (else that point would lie in $H(S)$ and in $D(S)$, contradicting $D(S)\cap H(S)=\varnothing$), so $D(S)$ is open around every point of $D(S)\setminus S$; at points of $S$ it is open because the boundary satisfies $\partial D(S)\cap S=\varnothing$: indeed the source's identity $H^\pm(S)\cap S=\mathrm{edge}(S)=\varnothing$ holds as $S$ is edgeless, and $\partial D(S)\setminus S\subseteq H(S)$. (iii) *Causal convexity.* [Minguzzi, Section 3: "Let $S$ be closed and achronal. The sets $\operatorname{Int}D(S)$, $\operatorname{Int}D^+(S)$ and $\operatorname{Int}D^-(S)$ are all causally convex", i.e. for $p,q\in\operatorname{Int}D(S)$ one has $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)\subseteq\operatorname{Int}D(S)$.] Since $D(S)=\operatorname{Int}D(S)$ by (ii), this is clause (b).

(The chronological-side property, proved from the definition.) Let $p\in D^+(S)\setminus S$. Choose a past-directed timelike geodesic segment $\beta_0:[0,1]\to W$ with $\beta_0(0)=p$ (in a chart at $p$, a small past- directed timelike geodesic exists by the time-orientation, [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). By [L3] let $\beta$ extend $\beta_0$ to a past-directed causal curve in $W$ that is past-inextendible in $W$ with $\beta(0)=p$; passing to the subcurve containing $\beta_0$ keeps the curve timelike on a nondegenerate interval, so $\beta$ is a past-directed past-inextendible **timelike** curve through $p$. Since $p\in D^+(S)$, $\beta$ meets $S$; at some parameter $t_s\le 0$. The subcurve of $\beta$ between $t_s$ and $0$ is a nondegenerate segment of a timelike curve joining $s:=\beta(t_s)\in S$ to $p$; if $s=p$ then $p\in S\cap(D^+(S)\setminus S)=\varnothing$, impossible, so $s\ne p$ and the segment is nondegenerate; by [L2] $s\ll p$, hence $p\in I^+(S)$. The time reverse gives $D^-(S)\setminus S\subseteq I^-(S)$. This proves the "moreover" part of clause (a).

(Disjointness of the chronological sides.) $S$ acausal implies $S$ achronal, and then $I^+(S)\cap I^-(S)=\varnothing$: points $s_1\ll x\ll s_2$ with $s_1,s_2\in S$ give $s_1\ll s_2$ by push-up [L2], contradicting achronality, and conversely every point of the intersection yields such a pair.

(Consequences for curves in $D(S)$.) Let $\gamma:I\to D(S)$ be a causal curve with $\gamma\cap S=\varnothing$. By step 2.1 every value of $\gamma$ lies in $I^+(S)\cup I^-(S)$, which by step 3.1 is a disjoint union of two open sets; by continuity of $\gamma$ on the interval $I$ ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) its image is connected, so the image lies entirely in one of the two sides.

(Proof of clause (c): every curve in $D(S)$ inextendible in $D(S)$ meets $S$.) Suppose, for contradiction, that $\gamma:I\to D(S)$ is a causal curve inextendible in $D(S)$ with $\gamma\cap S=\varnothing$. By step 4.1 we may assume $\gamma\subseteq I^-(S)$ (the other case is the time reverse, with the roles of $D^+$ and $D^-$ interchanged). Since $D^+(S)\setminus S\subseteq I^+(S)$ by step 2.1, no value of $\gamma$ lies in $D^+(S)\setminus S$, and no value lies in $S$; hence $\gamma\subseteq D^-(S)$.

(An extension past the future end.) Fix $t_0\in I$ and put $p:=\gamma(t_0)\in D^-(S)$. By [L3] extend $\gamma$ to a causal curve $\beta:J\to W$ that is future-inextendible in $W$, with $J\supseteq I$ an interval. By the definition of $D^-(S)$, the future-directed future-inextendible causal curve $\beta$ from $p$ meets $S$: there is $\tau\in J$, $\tau\ge t_0$, with $\beta(\tau)\in S$.

(The meeting cannot lie beyond $I$; exclusion of $y\in S$.) Suppose $	au

otin S$: if $y\in S$, then either $b\in I$, in which case $y=\gamma(b)\in S$ contradicts $\gamma\cap S=\varnothing$, or $b
otin I$, in which case adjoining the value $y\in S\subseteq D(S)$ at the parameter $b$ exhibits a causal curve in $D(S)$, on the strictly larger interval $I\cup\{b\}$, extending $\gamma$ (continuous, with causal velocity almost everywhere), contradicting inextendibility of $\gamma$ in $D(S)$.

(The limit point lies in the timelike past domain.) Each $\gamma(t)$ lies in $D^-(S)\subseteq\widetilde D^-(S)$, and $\widetilde D^-(S)$ is closed by [L1]. Since $\gamma(t)\to y$, we get $y\in\widetilde D^-(S)$.

(The limit point lies in $D^-(S)$.) Suppose $y\notin D^-(S)$: then there is a future-directed causal curve $\alpha:[0,c)\to W$ with $\alpha(0)=y$, future-inextendible in $W$, whose image misses $S$. Choose $s_0\in I$ with $s_0<b$. The concatenation $\delta:=\beta|_{[s_0,b]}\cup\alpha$, glued at the common value $y$, is a future-directed causal curve in $W$ starting at $\gamma(s_0)$ that is future-inextendible in $W$ (its future end agrees with that of $\alpha$) and whose image misses $S$: the $\beta$-part consists of values of $\gamma$, which misses $S$ by hypothesis; the joint value $y$ is not in $S$ by step 7.1; and the $\alpha$-part misses $S$ by construction. But $\gamma(s_0)\in D^-(S)$, and by definition every future-directed future-inextendible causal curve in $W$ from a point of $D^-(S)$ meets $S$. This contradiction proves $y\in D^-(S)\subseteq D(S)$.

(The final contradiction.) By step 9.1, $y\in D(S)$; by step 6.1, $\sigma:=\beta(\tau)\in S\subseteq D(S)$. The segment $\beta|_{[b,\tau]}$ is a causal curve with both endpoints in $D(S)$, so by clause (b) (Step 1.1(iii)) its image is contained in $D(S)$. Hence the concatenation $\gamma\cup\beta|_{[b,\tau]}$ is a causal curve on the strictly larger interval $I\cup[b,\tau]$, contained in $D(S)$, extending $\gamma$. This contradicts inextendibility of $\gamma$ in $D(S)$. Therefore every causal curve in $D(S)$ inextendible in $D(S)$ meets $S$.

(Exactly once.) By step 10.1 such a curve meets $S$ at least once. If it met $S$ at two distinct parameter values $t_1<t_2$, the subcurve on $[t_1,t_2]$ would be a causal curve in $W$ from $\gamma(t_1)\in S$ to the distinct point $\gamma(t_2)\in S$, contradicting acausality of $S$ [L2]. Hence the meeting is unique, which completes clause (c).

Statement: quantities that may vanish are treated explicitly or excluded by the stated positivity and nondegeneracy hypotheses; no step divides by a quantity that can be zero outside the stated exclusions.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data and
let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$C\subseteq\partial U$ be the set of boundary points that have a corresponding
point (clause (c) of that definition), and write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. If
$C\cap J^+(\Sigma)\neq\varnothing$, then there exists $p\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$
with
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$ for
   some $t_y\in(-\delta(s),\delta(s))$, and the radial segment with the base
   point removed,
   $\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$, is contained in
   $U$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in I^-(p)\cap U$ and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their first
covariant derivatives along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(W,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$S\subseteq W$ be a **partial Cauchy hypersurface**: a closed, acausal,
edgeless embedded topological hypersurface of codimension one
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], the edge being defined as
in the cited source). Write $I^\pm(S)$, $J^\pm(S)$ for the chronological and
causal future and past of $S$ in $W$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) and let
$$D^\pm(S):=\{p\in W:\ \text{every past- (respectively future-) inextendible causal curve in }W\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$$
be the **causal domains of dependence of $S$ in $W$**. Then:

**(a)** $D(S)$ is open in $W$ and $S\subseteq D(S)$; moreover
$D^\pm(S)\setminus S\subseteq I^\pm(S)$, so every point of $D(S)\setminus S$
lies on one of the two chronological sides of $S$;

**(b)** $D(S)$ is **causally convex**: every causal curve in $W$ whose
endpoints lie in $D(S)$ is contained in $D(S)$;

**(c)** $S$ is a Cauchy set of the open submanifold $(D(S),g|_{D(S)})$: every
causal curve in $D(S)$ that is inextendible in $D(S)$ meets $S$ in exactly one
parameter value.

**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.
The concrete sectors used later in this batch are the vacuum sector ($s=0$,
$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed

Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let

chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$ for
   some $t_y\in(-\delta(s),\delta(s))$, and the radial segment with the base
   point removed,
   $\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$, is contained in
   $U$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$ and with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ (so $\varphi$ is an isometric immersion fixing the data).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$, that is, $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$ and $d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)$
for every $q\in N$.

**(b) Data-fixing embeddings have equal differentials on the initial surface.**
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be
as in [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a),
and let $\psi_1,\psi_2:U\to M'$ be development embeddings in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c). Then
$d\psi_1=d\psi_2$ at every point of $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$.

**(c) Agreement on overlaps.** Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$
be developments of the same data, and let $(U_1,\psi_1)$ and $(U_2,\psi_2)$ be
common subdevelopments in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $U_1\cap U_2$.

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let

([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$ for
   some $t_y\in(-\delta(s),\delta(s))$, and the radial segment with the base
   point removed,
   $\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$, is contained in
   $U$.

**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.

$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

derivations.claim:
(Reduction to $C\cap J^+(\Sigma)
e\varnothing$; time reversal.) Suppose $C
e\varnothing$; by time reversal of the two developments (which exchanges $j(\Sigma)$-future and past and preserves all hypotheses) we may assume $C\cap J^+(\Sigma)
e\varnothing$. Then [L1] provides the exposed point $p$ and the whole restart configuration.

(The local uniqueness isometry.) By [L2] the complete Cauchy data of $S$ are realized in $M$ (by the inclusion $S\hookrightarrow M$) and in $M'$ (by $\Phi|_S$). By [L4] there is a development $D(S)\subseteq W^\circ$ of these data with Cauchy surface $S$; and applying clause (d) of [[lem-gr-local-cauchy-neighborhood]] to the smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Phi(S)\subseteq M'$ (a smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface without boundary, [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] clause (e) and [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] clause (b)) gives a globally hyperbolic open neighbourhood $W_{\Phi(S)}$ of $\Phi(S)$ in $M'$ on which $\Phi(S)$ is Cauchy, hence a development of the same data with initial embedding $\Phi|_S$. The local geometric development theorem [L3] applied to these two developments yields an open neighbourhood $O\subseteq D(S)$ of $S$ and a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry $\varphi:O\to M'$ onto an open subset of $W_{\Phi(S)}$ with $\varphi|_S=\Phi|_S$ and matching all matter fields. Replace $O$ by $O\cap N$ (still an open neighbourhood of $S$, as $S\subseteq N$).

(A radial sub-tube of $O$.) Choose a continuous positive width function $\delta_0\le\delta$ on $S$ such that $\delta_0$ is Lipschitz-small with respect to the level metrics, vanishes toward the ends of $S$, and $F(s,t)\in O$ for every $|t|<\delta_0(s)$: for instance $\delta_0:=\varepsilon\min(\delta,\rho,\operatorname{dist}_h(\cdot,M\setminus O))$ with $\rho$ as in [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] and $\varepsilon>0$ small. Put $N_0:=F(S\times(-\delta_0,\delta_0))$. Then $N_0\subseteq O\cap N$ is an open radial tube over $S$.

($\psi=\varphi$ on $N_0\cap U$.) Let $y\in N_0\cap U$; write $y=F(s,t_y)$ with $s\in S$ and $|t_y|<\delta_0(s)$, and let $\gamma$ be the flow line through $s$ (a geodesic segment through $y$, [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] [L3]). By [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] clause (c)3 the radial segment from $s$ to $y$ (excluding $s$) is contained in $U$. Hence $\psi\circ\gamma$ is a geodesic of $M'$ on the parameter interval between $s$ and $y$ ([[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (a)), and so is $\varphi\circ\gamma$ (as $\gamma\subseteq N_0\subseteq O$). At $s$ the two curves have the same limiting value and velocity: the value is $\Phi(s)=\varphi(s)$ (step 2.1) and the velocity is $d\varphi_s(\gamma'(s))=d\Phi_s(\gamma'(s))$, because $\varphi|_S=\Phi|_S$ gives equality on $T_sS$, and both differentials are isometries carrying the unit future normal of $S$ to the unit future normal of $\Phi(S)$ ([[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] clause (e); [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]] for the uniqueness of the normal). By uniqueness of geodesics with given initial data ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]) the two geodesics coincide, so $\psi(y)=\varphi(y)$.

(The patched map.) Define $\Psi:U\cup N_0\to M'$ by $\Psi:=\psi$ on $U$ and $\Psi:=\varphi$ on $N_0$. This is well defined by step 4.1 and smooth and is a data-fixing isometric immersion preserving the time orientation and the matter fields, because these are local properties and hold for $\psi$ on $U$ and for $\varphi$ on $N_0$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c), [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)).

($U\cup N_0$ is a development.) By [L6] every causal curve in $U\cup N_0$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N_0$ meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; $U\cup N_0\subseteq M$ is open with the restricted metric, time orientation and matter fields, the field equations hold (they are local and hold on $M$), and $j:\Sigma\to U\cup N_0$ is an embedding with the induced data $(h,K,\psi_0)$. Hence $U\cup N_0$ is a development of the same data ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)); in particular it is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $\Sigma$ by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

($\Psi$ is a development embedding.) By step 5.1, $\Psi$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $U\cup N_0$ into $M'$; hence it is injective and a diffeomorphism onto the open set $\Psi(U\cup N_0)$ by [L5].

(Strictly larger.) Pick $x\in S\cap\partial U$ (nonempty by [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] clause (b)). Then $x\in S\subseteq N_0$ and $x\notin U$, so $N_0\not\subseteq U$ and $U\subsetneq U\cup N_0$. Thus $(U\cup N_0,\Psi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ strictly larger than $(U,\varphi)$, contradicting the maximality of $(U,\varphi)$ assumed in the statement.
(Conclusion.) Therefore the assumption $C\ne\varnothing$ is false: $C=\varnothing$.
