equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open matter domain
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **perfect-fluid model** on $U$ is a triple $(\varepsilon,p,n)$
consisting of two smooth functions $\varepsilon,p:U\to\mathbb R$, the **rest
energy density** and the **pressure**, and a smooth future-directed unit
timelike vector field $n$ on $U$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and
$g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). No positivity of
$\varepsilon$ or of $p$ is required or implied. A model may carry the
additional data of an **equation of state**: a function
$P:D_P\to\mathbb R$ on a subset $D_P\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$\varepsilon(U)\subseteq D_P$, together with the relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$;
the relation is a further assumption and is not part of the basic triple.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor and derived fields.** The model's
**stress-energy tensor** is

$$T^{ab}:=(\varepsilon+p)n^an^b+p\,g^{ab},$$

a smooth symmetric contravariant $2$-tensor field ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). The **comoving
derivative**, **expansion** and **acceleration** of $n$ are

$$D f:=n^a\partial_af\quad(f\in C^\infty(U)),\qquad \vartheta:=\nabla_an^a,\qquad a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b ,$$

and the **rest-space projection** is the smooth tensor field

$$h^{ab}:=g^{ab}+n^an^b .$$

The physical reading of $\varepsilon$ and $p$ as a rest-frame energy density
and pressure, and their units, are fixed by the framework's matter postulate,
not by this definition.

**(c) Fluid equations.** The **perfect-fluid equations** on $U$ are

$$D\varepsilon+(\varepsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\varepsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0 .$$

That the stress-energy tensor is divergence-free if and only if these two
equations hold is proved in
[[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; the definition
asserts neither divergence-freedom nor the equations.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The physical reading of $\rho$ as a rest-mass density in a unit system, and of
$u$ as the four-velocity congruence of the matter, is fixed by the framework's
matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and $c>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the abstract bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(N+v_0)$, as specified in [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]];
4. **geodesic dust:** an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon_0\ge0$
   with prescribed smooth future unit velocity $U_0$, as a section of
   $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $-ab+h(X,Y)$.
   On positive-density regions this is the model $(\varepsilon,u)$ of
   [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; through zero-density regions its smooth
   unit velocity is separately prescribed and required to remain geodesic.
   Its source is $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$\kappa>0$, let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, and let smooth
matter initial data be given in one of the four branches (vacuum with
cosmological constant, scalar field, strict barotropic perfect fluid,
geodesic dust) of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]], with
the constraint equations satisfied, so that at least one development of the
data exists. Then there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of the data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
clause (a) that is maximal in the sense of clause (d) of that definition:
for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data there is a
data-fixing development embedding $M\to M_{\mathrm{max}}$. Moreover, if
$(M'_{\mathrm{max}},g'_{\mathrm{max}},N'_{\mathrm{max}},j'_{\mathrm{max}},\psi'_{\mathrm{max}})$
is another maximal development of the same data, then there is exactly one
data-fixing isometry $M_{\mathrm{max}}\to M'_{\mathrm{max}}$; the maximal
development is thus unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry. It is
connected and, by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]],
globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.
The concrete sectors used later in this batch are the vacuum sector ($s=0$,
$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and Einstein tensor $G$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)), and fix real
constants $\kappa$ and $\Lambda$ (the framework coupling constants, purely
parameters for this definition).

**(a) The geometric data.**
For $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is
one-dimensional and nondegenerate
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]],
[[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]); there is therefore a unique
$n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with $g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$ and it
depends smoothly on $p$, the **future unit normal field** of $\Sigma$; this
and the properties of $h$ and $K$ below are proved, not assumed, in
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]. Define
on $\Sigma$ the **induced metric** $h$ and the **second fundamental form**
$K$ by
$$h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W),\qquad K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma),$$
where $\nabla_Vn$ is the covariant derivative at $p$ of the ambient field $n$
in the tangential direction $V$; $h$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(b) Matter data and constraints.** Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ (the stress-energy field of a matter branch). Its
**matter data on $\Sigma$** are the smooth fields
$$\rho:=T(n,n),\qquad j(V):=-T(n,V)\quad(V\in T\Sigma).$$
The tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ **satisfies the constraint equations** for
$(\kappa,\Lambda)$ when
$$G(n,n)-\Lambda=\kappa\,\rho,\qquad G(n,V)=\kappa\,T(n,V)\quad\text{for every }V\in T_p\Sigma,\ p\in\Sigma .$$
The first is the normal projection of the equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$
evaluated on $(n,n)$, namely $G(n,n)+\Lambda g(n,n)=\kappa T(n,n)$, with
$g(n,n)=-1$; the second is the normal-tangential projection, the term in
$\Lambda$ dropping because $g(n,V)=0$. That a solution of the field equation
satisfies these two projections is proved in
[[lem-gr-constraint-projections]]. The purely tangential projection
$G(V,W)+\Lambda h(V,W)=\kappa T(V,W)$ is not part of the constraints and is
not required here.

**(c) Developments.** A **development** of the data
$(\Sigma,h,K,\rho,j)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
$(M',g',N')$ together with a smooth embedding $\varphi:\Sigma\to M'$ whose
image is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\varphi^*g'=h$
and second fundamental form $K$ with respect to the future unit normal of
$\varphi(\Sigma)$, such that the matter fields of the model pull back to
$\rho$ and $j$. The development is a **globally hyperbolic development** when
$\varphi(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(M',g',N')$, so that
$(M',g',N')$ is globally hyperbolic
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]],
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)).

**(d) Maximality.** A globally hyperbolic development $(M_*,g_*,N_*;
\varphi_*)$ is **maximal** for the data when for every globally hyperbolic
development $(M',g',N';\varphi')$ there is a smooth isometric embedding
$\psi:M'\to M_*$ with $\psi\circ\varphi'=\varphi_*$ and $\psi$ preserving the
time orientations and the matter fields. Thus maximality is uniqueness up to
data-fixing isometry among globally hyperbolic developments.

**(e) Scope.** The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of
developments, and it does not assert that a development's matter fields solve
any equation: those claims require the local and global existence theory of
the Einstein-matter system and are not made on this page. The constraint
equations are displayed only as equations satisfied or not by given data.
The equivalent formulation of the constraints in terms of the induced scalar
curvature of $h$ and the divergence of $K$, and the existence theory for
solutions of the constraints, rest on the Gauss-Codazzi relations and on PDE
theory and are deferred to the later pages of this track; no such
equivalence is asserted here.

derivations.claim: (Relating the postulates to the mathematical model.) By [F1] and [F2] the field law and matter equations of the model are exactly the Einstein-matter system of the four sectors of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]], with the same regularity requirements. By [A1] the constraint equations are the model's compatibility conditions on the data.
(Existence of at least one development.) Under the hypotheses on the data the reduction hypotheses hold, so by [F3] the data admit at least one smooth development within the model's equations.

(The maximal development exists and is unique.) Applying [F4] with step 2.1 as the nonemptiness input, the data have a maximal development $(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$ which is unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry, and every development embeds into it. This is (a) and (b).

(Global hyperbolicity.) By [F4] the maximal development is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$; hence the model's initial-value problem restricted to the constraint-satisfying data is deterministic: two iterations of the same data are isometric fixing the initial surface. This is (c).

(Conditional character and scope.) The chain of steps 1.1-4.1 is a conditional deduction: each physical ingredient enters only through the adopted postulates [F1]-[F2], and each mathematical step is a theorem with explicitly stated hypotheses. The deduction establishes no statement about the physical universe and no observational claim; if a sector's regularity assumptions or the constraint equations fail for data of interest, the deduction does not apply. This completes the proof of the conditional assertion.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$\kappa>0$, let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, and let smooth
matter initial data be given in one of the four branches (vacuum with
cosmological constant, scalar field, strict barotropic perfect fluid,
geodesic dust) of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]], with
the constraint equations satisfied, so that at least one development of the
data exists. Then there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of the data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
clause (a) that is maximal in the sense of clause (d) of that definition:
for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data there is a
data-fixing development embedding $M\to M_{\mathrm{max}}$. Moreover, if
$(M'_{\mathrm{max}},g'_{\mathrm{max}},N'_{\mathrm{max}},j'_{\mathrm{max}},\psi'_{\mathrm{max}})$
is another maximal development of the same data, then there is exactly one
data-fixing isometry $M_{\mathrm{max}}\to M'_{\mathrm{max}}$; the maximal
development is thus unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry. It is
connected and, by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]],
globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$ and with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ (so $\varphi$ is an isometric immersion fixing the data).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and curvature $R$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let $p\in M$, let
$\mathcal E_p\subseteq T_pM$ be the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], let $W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
be a star-shaped open neighborhood of $0$ on which $\exp_p$ is a
diffeomorphism onto the open set $U:=\exp_p(W)$, and suppose

$$R\equiv0\quad\text{on }U .$$

Let $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be a $g_p$-orthonormal basis of $T_pM$ and
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ its coordinate isomorphism, and write
$\eta_{ab}:=g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]).

**(a) The differential of the exponential map is an isometry.** For every
$v\in W$ the differential
$d(\exp_p)_v:\bigl(T_pM,g_p\bigr)\to\bigl(T_{\exp_p(v)}M,g_{\exp_p(v)}\bigr)$
is a linear isometry ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]).

**(b) Local isometry.** The map $\exp_p:(W,g_p)\to(U,g)$ is an isometry of
the open subset $W$ of the flat vector space $(T_pM,g_p)$ onto $(U,g)$;
equivalently $\exp_p^*g=g_p$ on $W$.

**(c) Constant metric components.** In the exponential chart
$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$, the components of $g$ are the
constants $g_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$; hence the identity map of $u(U)$ with the
standard Minkowski form is an isometry of $U$ onto an open subset of
Minkowski space.

**(d) Open flat sets.** If $R\equiv0$ on an open set $O\subseteq M$ and
$p\in O$, then there is a star-shaped open $W_0\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ with
$\exp_p(W_0)\subseteq O$ for which (a)-(c) hold; in particular every point of
$O$ has a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of Minkowski space.

**(e) Converse direction.** Conversely, if an open set $V\subseteq M$ admits
a smooth chart in which $g_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$ are constant, then $R\equiv0$ on
$V$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

derivations.claim: (Minkowski is a development of the data.) On $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=-dt^2+\delta$ the curvature vanishes, so the Einstein tensor vanishes and $G+\Lambda\eta=0=\kappa\cdot0$: the vacuum field equation holds ([[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]] records the flat case). The slice $\{t=0\}$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\delta$ and vanishing second fundamental form, since the unit normal $\partial_t$ is parallel; and every inextendible causal curve in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ meets $\{t=0\}$ exactly once, because its $t$-coordinate is a nondecreasing unbounded function changing sign ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Hence $(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta,\partial_t,j)$ is a development of the data.

(It is maximal.) By [[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]] the data have a maximal development, unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry, and every development embeds into it by a data-fixing development embedding. Since Minkowski is a development of the data by step 1.1, it is (up to that unique data-fixing isometry) the maximal development; in particular the class of developments of the flat vacuum data is exactly the class of data-fixing embeddings of open subsets into Minkowski, by [[lem-gr-data-fixing-immersion-is-embedding]] clauses (b)-(c).

citations.quote:
**Data.** Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, so that $\Sigma$ is
Hausdorff, second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$,
let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$, and let a **matter sector** be specified
as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a finite list of tensor types
$r_1,\dots,r_s$, a smooth **stress-energy construction** $T(g,\psi)$, a smooth
covariant symmetric $2$-tensor field built from a Lorentzian metric $g$ and
fields $\psi=(\psi^1,\dots,\psi^s)$ of the listed types on a four-manifold
carrying $\Sigma$, and a system $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that in every chart the
combined system for $(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] is a first-order quasilinear
symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on shell. Let smooth **matter initial data**
$\psi_0$ on $\Sigma$ be given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] clause (d) hold on
$\Sigma$, with $n$ the future unit normal and $T$ determined by $(h,K,\psi_0)$.
The concrete sectors used later in this batch are the vacuum sector ($s=0$,
$T=0$), the scalar-field sector ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), the
strict barotropic perfect-fluid sector ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]])
and the geodesic-dust sector ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); no other sector is
asserted here.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. smooth sections $\psi^i$ of the tensor bundles over $M$ of the types
   $r_i$ of the sector;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $\psi_0$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $d\varphi_p(N_p)=N'_{\varphi(p)}$ for every $p\in M$, so $\varphi$ carries
   the time orientation of $N$ to that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, that is, $\psi'{}^i(\varphi(p))=(d\varphi_p)^{\otimes}\psi^i(p)$
   for every $i$ and $p$, with the natural action on tensor fields of each
   listed type.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,\psi_0)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

Take $\Sigma:=\mathbb R^3$, $h$ the Euclidean metric $\delta$, $K:=0$,
$\Lambda:=0$, $\kappa>0$ and the vacuum sector of
[[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]] (no matter fields,
$T=0$); the constraint equations reduce to $0=0$ and are satisfied. Then
the maximal development of these data is, up to a unique data-fixing
isometry, four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
$(\mathbb R^4,\eta)=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the standard initial
embedding $j:M\to\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $j(x)=(0,x)$, and time orientation
$N=\partial_t$.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

**(a) Common subdevelopment.** A **common subdevelopment** of $M$ and $M'$ is
a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

Here "the induced field equations on $U$" means the equations of clause (a)4
of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Maximal common development.** A common subdevelopment $(U^*,\varphi^*)$
is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

**(c) Corresponding boundary points.** Let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common
subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

**(d) Side of the initial surface.** For a corresponding pair $(p,p')$: if
$V,V'$ range over a base of neighbourhoods, the condition of (c) forces every
$x$ witnessing it to lie on one side of $j(\Sigma)$: either $x\in I^+(j(\Sigma))$
for cofinally many witnesses, or $x\in I^-(j(\Sigma))$ for cofinally many
witnesses, but not both, since $I^\pm(j(\Sigma))$ are open and determined by
the trichotomy of [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]]. The corresponding
pair is then said to lie to the **future** or to the **past** of the initial
surface; the future case is the one used in this batch, the past case being
its time reverse.

**(e) Scope.** These are mathematical relations between two fixed developments
and their boundary points. Neither the existence of boundary points, nor the
existence of a common subdevelopment with nonempty boundary, nor uniqueness of
a corresponding point, is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a),
with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. Then there exist $U^*\subseteq M$ and
$\psi^*:U^*\to M'$ such that:

**(a)** $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ in the sense
of [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a);

**(b)** for every common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ and $M'$ one has
$U\subseteq U^*$ and $\psi^*|_U=\varphi$; in particular $(U^*,\psi^*)$ is a
maximal common development in the sense of clause (b) of that definition, and
it contains $j(\Sigma)$;

**(c)** uniqueness: if $(U^\dagger,\psi^\dagger)$ also satisfies (a) and (b),
then $U^\dagger=U^*$ and $\psi^\dagger=\psi^*$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the countable atlases in (b). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, and let $(U,\varphi)$ be their
maximal common development
([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (b),
[[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]]). Let
$Z:=(M\sqcup M',\tau)$ be the topological disjoint union with canonical
inclusions $\iota_M:M\to Z$, $\iota_{M'}:M'\to Z$, and define a relation $\sim$ on
$Z$ by: $z\sim w$ when $z=w$, or $z=\iota_M(p)$ and $w=\iota_{M'}(\varphi(p))$ for
some $p\in U$, or $z=\iota_{M'}(p)$ and $w=\iota_M(\varphi^{-1}(p))$ for some
$p\in\varphi(U)$. Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi:Z\to Q$ and
quotient topology ([[def-quotient-topology]]). Then:

**(a)** $\sim$ is an equivalence relation; $\pi\circ\iota_M:M\to Q$ and
$\pi\circ\iota_{M'}:M'\to Q$ are injective, continuous and open, hence
homeomorphisms onto the open subsets $(\pi\circ\iota_M)(M)$ and
$(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(M')$, which cover $Q$;
$(\pi\circ\iota_M)(U)=(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(\varphi(U))=(\pi\circ\iota_M)(M)\cap(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(M')$;
and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(b)** $Q$ carries a unique structure of a second countable smooth
four-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) making $\pi\circ\iota_M$ and
$\pi\circ\iota_{M'}$ diffeomorphisms onto open subsets; a unique smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, time orientation $\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ on $Q$
making both maps isometries that preserve the time orientation and the matter
fields. These satisfy the field equations of the data on $Q$, and
$\bar j:=\pi\circ\iota_M\circ j$ is an embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data
$(h,K,\psi_0)$, so $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the
data; moreover every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in $Q$ meets
$\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value.

**(c)** $\Psi:=\pi\circ\iota_M$ and $\Psi':=\pi\circ\iota_{M'}$ are data-fixing
development embeddings of $M$ and $M'$ into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

derivations.claim: ($\psi$ is a data-fixing isometry.) The translation $\psi$ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ preserving $\eta$, the time orientation and (vacuously) the matter fields, and $\psi\circ j=j'$ by definition of $j,j'$. Hence $\psi:M\to M'$ is a development embedding of the whole of $M$, and $(M,\psi)$ is a common subdevelopment ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c), [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)).

(Maximality.) By [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] the maximal common development $(U^*,\psi^*)$ contains every common subdevelopment, so $U^*=M$ and $\psi^*=\psi$ by step 1.1 applied to $(U^*,\psi^*)$ in the reverse direction. In particular $U$ has no boundary in $M$, hence no corresponding boundary points, in accordance with [[lem-gr-no-corresponding-boundary-points]]. This is (a).

(The quotient.) By [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] the quotient $Q:=(M\sqcup M')/{\sim}$ with the identifications along $\psi$ is a development of the data and the maps $p_M,p_{M'}$ are data-fixing development embeddings; here every point of $M$ is identified with its image in $M'$ and conversely, so the canonical map $M\to Q$, $p\mapsto[p]$, is a bijection and an isometry: its inverse is the map sending the class of $m\in M$ to $m$ and the class of $m'\in M'$ to $\psi^{-1}(m')$, which is well defined because $m'\sim\psi^{-1}(m')$ and because $\psi$ is a bijection. Both compositions with $\eta$ agree, so $Q$ is isometric to $M$ by a data-fixing isometry; the two development embeddings are the identity and the inverse translation. This is (b).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
globally hyperbolic time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)), let
$L_g$ be the Lorentzian length functional on future causal curves
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), and for $q\in M$ define the
**time separation**
$$\tau_q:M\to[0,\infty),\qquad \tau_q(r):=\sup\{L_g(\alpha):\ \alpha \text{ is a future causal curve from } r \text{ to } q\},$$
the supremum over the empty set being $0$; thus $\tau_q(r)>0$ exactly for
$r\in I^-(q)$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\notin J^-(q)$.

**(a)** For every $r\in J^-(q)$ one has $0\le\tau_q(r)<\infty$, and the
supremum is attained: there is a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$
with $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. Every such **maximizer** is, up to monotone
reparametrization, a causal geodesic, and its image lies in the compact set
$J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$.

**(b)** Let $V$ be a strictly convex normal neighbourhood of $q$ (as produced
by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and let $W\subseteq V$ be open and
causally convex in $M$ (every causal curve in $M$ with both endpoints in $W$
is contained in $W$), with $\overline W$ compact and $q\in W$. Then for every
$r\in W\cap I^-(q)$,
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q\bigl(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r)\bigr)},$$
so $\tau_q$ is smooth on $W\cap I^-(q)$ and extends continuously by
$\tau_q(q)=0$ and $\tau_q(r)=0$ for $r\in W\setminus J^-(q)$.

**(c)** On every compact set $K\subseteq M$ the function $\tau_q$ is upper
semicontinuous in the following strong form: for every sequence $r_n\to r$ in
$K$ one has $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\tau_q(r)$. If moreover $r\in I^-(q)$,
then $\tau_q(r_n)\to\tau_q(r)$ for every sequence $r_n\to r$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the pointwise causal
classification of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] and the
equivalence of "future-directed" with "pairing negatively with $N$" supplied by
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]. All curves below
take values in $M$; the physical reading of the model is not part of this
definition.

**(a) The curve class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A **chart
representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ of a smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). The map $\gamma$ is
**locally absolutely continuous** when for every compact subinterval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$ and every chart $(U,x)$ with
$\gamma([a,b])\subseteq U$, the component map $x\circ\gamma$ is absolutely
continuous on $[a,b]$ in the sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]].
This class does not depend on the chart or on the smooth atlas; that is proved
in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (a).

**(b) Velocity and causal curves.** Let $\gamma$ be locally absolutely
continuous and let $t$ be an interior point of $I$ at which some — equivalently
every — chart representative is differentiable. The **velocity**
$\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation whose components in a chart
$(U,x)$ around $\gamma(t)$ are
$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}(x^a\circ\gamma)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)}$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]],
[[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]); it is independent of the
chart by the chain rule, as recorded in
[[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (b). A **future causal curve** is a
locally absolutely continuous $\gamma$ such that the set of $t\in I$ for which
$\gamma'(t)$ exists, is nonzero and is future causal is of full measure in
$I$ (its complement meets every compact subinterval of $I$ in a set of
Lebesgue measure zero). A **future timelike curve** (also called future
chronological) is defined in the same way with "future causal" replaced by
"future timelike". Past-directed versions are defined with $g_p(v,N_p)>0$.
Since a future causal nonzero vector is nonzero by definition, the velocity is
required to be nonzero at almost every parameter value; in particular no
nondegenerate subinterval of $I$ can be mapped to a single point
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (c)).

**(c) Reachability.** For events $p,q\in M$ define:

- $p\le q$, read "$q$ is in the future of $p$", when $p=q$, or when there are
  $a<b$ and a future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$;
- $p\ll q$, read "$p$ chronologically precedes $q$", when there are $a<b$ and
  a future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=p$ and
  $\gamma(b)=q$.

The **causal future** and **chronological future** of a subset $S\subseteq M$
are
$$J^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}J^+(p),\qquad I^+(S):=\bigcup_{p\in S}I^+(p),$$
where $J^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\le q\}$ and $I^+(p):=\{q\in M:p\ll q\}$; past
versions are $J^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\in J^+(q)\}$ and
$I^-(S):=\{p:\exists q\in S,\ p\ll q\}$. By the displayed definition
$p\in J^+(p)$ for every $p$. Whether $p\in I^+(p)$ is a property of the
model, not a convention: $p\ll p$ holds exactly when there are $a<b$ and a
future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)=p$, that
is, exactly when a closed future timelike curve through $p$ exists. No
irreflexivity of $\ll$ is asserted, and closed timelike curves are not
excluded by the definition.

**(d) Inextendibility.** A locally absolutely continuous causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ is **future-inextendible** when $\gamma$ does not converge to
any point of $M$ as its parameter tends to $\sup I$, that is, there is no
$x\in M$ with $\gamma(t)\to x$ as $t\to\sup I$; in particular a curve whose
parameter range is unbounded above is future-inextendible exactly when it does
not converge as $t\to+\infty$. **Past-inextendible** is defined dually with
$\inf I$, and $\gamma$ is **inextendible** when it is both. This is the
convention of Minguzzi's Definition 2.16; for causal curves parametrized by
arclength of a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric it agrees with "the domain
cannot be extended", and a causal curve that converges at an endpoint can be
extended by a short geodesic segment, as proved in
[[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clauses (a) and (b). A causal
curve **passes through** $p$ when $p\in\gamma(I)$.

**(e) Scope.** The definitions are mathematical. They record no postulate
about nature, no measurement and no dynamical law; the physical reading of
$(M,g,N)$ and of the causal structure as the model's signalling structure is
adopted in the framework postulates and is not asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the
causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], and let
$S\subseteq M$.

**(a) Spacelike hypersurfaces.** A subset $\Sigma\subseteq M$ is a **spacelike
embedded hypersurface** when it is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
of $M$ ([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) such that the
restriction of $g_p$ to $T_p\Sigma\times T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for
every $p\in\Sigma$; equivalently, every nonzero vector tangent to $\Sigma$ is
spacelike ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). A spacelike
embedded hypersurface is automatically a nondegenerate hypersurface, so its
$g$-orthogonal complement in $T_pM$ is one-dimensional and nondegenerate, and
it carries a unique future-directed unit timelike normal; that normal is
constructed where it is used, not here.

**(b) Achronality and acausality.** $S$ is **achronal** when no two distinct
points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\ll q$ or $q\ll p$; $S$ is **acausal** when no two
distinct points $p,q\in S$ satisfy $p\le q$ or $q\le p$. Every acausal set is
achronal, since $p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$.

**(c) Cauchy sets.** $S$ is a **Cauchy set** when for every inextendible
causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ the parameter set
$$\gamma^{-1}[S]:=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$$
has exactly one element. Because a strictly increasing continuous surjection
of intervals induces a bijection of parameter sets, this condition is
invariant under reparametrization
([[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]] clause (e)); it is stated in terms of
parameters rather than of the point set $\gamma(I)\cap S$, so that a closed
causal curve counts two visits to the same point as two parameter values. A
**Cauchy hypersurface** is a Cauchy set that is also a spacelike embedded
hypersurface in the sense of clause (a).

**(d) Domains of dependence.** For any $S\subseteq M$ define
$$D^+(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve through }p \text{ meets }S\},$$
and dually $D^-(S):=\{p\in M:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve
through }p\text{ meets }S\}$, where "meets $S$" means that some parameter
value is mapped into $S$, and $D(S):=D^+(S)\cup D^-(S)$ is the **domain of
dependence** of $S$.

**(e) Cauchy horizon.** For a closed set $S\subseteq M$ the **future Cauchy
horizon** is
$$H^+(S):=D^+(S)\setminus I^-(D^+(S)),$$
the set of points of $D^+(S)$ that are not chronologically preceded by any
point of $D^+(S)$; dually $H^-(S):=D^-(S)\setminus I^+(D^-(S))$, and the
**Cauchy horizon** is $H(S):=H^+(S)\cup H^-(S)$.

**(f) Scope.** These are mathematical definitions. Neither existence of
Cauchy sets nor any relation between the objects defined here is asserted.

derivations.claim: (The distance formula.) For $r\in J^-(q)$ the displacement $q-r=(\Delta t,\Delta x)$ is causal, and the unique maximizer of the Lorentzian length from $r$ to $q$ is the straight timelike segment, whose length is $\sqrt{-(\Delta t)^2+|\Delta x|^2}=\sqrt{(t-1)^2-|x|^2}$ when the displacement is timelike; for lightlike displacement the value is $0$; this is the Minkowski instance of the attainability and geodesy of maximizers in [[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clause (a).

(Smoothness and spacality.) On the open set $U:=\{r:\tau_q(r)>0\}=I^-(q)$ the function $f(t,x):=(t-1)^2-|x|^2$ is smooth with gradient $2((t-1),-x)$, which is timelike on $U$ (there $(t-1)^2>|x|^2$); hence its level set $\{f=\tau_0^2\}$, which is $S$, is a smooth embedded hypersurface with timelike normal and is therefore spacelike ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

(At most one meeting along a causal curve.) Since $\tau_q$ is continuous and $g(\nabla\tau_q,\cdot)$ has no nonzero causal kernel on $U$, the function $t\mapsto\tau_q(\gamma(t))$ is strictly monotone along every causal curve segment contained in $U$; hence such a segment meets the level $\tau_0$ in at most one parameter value, and a causal curve segment with $\tau_q$-values straddling $\tau_0$ meets $S$ at least once by the intermediate value theorem ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clause (b), [[def-continuity-real]]). If a causal curve met $S$ in two parameter values, the subsegment between them would join two points of $S$ with equal $\tau_q$-value, contradicting strict monotonicity; if the subsegment left $U$ it would contain a point $p$ with $\tau_q(p)=0$, that is $p\not\ll q$; but $p\le\gamma(t_2)\ll q$ and push-up gives $p\ll q$, a contradiction ([[lem-gr-push-up-rule]], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

(Radial description.) For $r=(1-\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},x_s)\in S$ the segment to $q$ is $s\mapsto q-\frac{s}{\tau_0}\bigl(\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},x_s\bigr)$, which is a geodesic with timelike velocity of constant norm $1$, hence a timelike geodesic of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$. Conversely every past endpoint of a timelike geodesic of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$ lies on $S$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ and the
family of member maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as
in [[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d), so that $Q$ is a
Hausdorff locally Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, the sets $Q_\alpha$ are open and cover $Q$, and
$\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$ is the embedded initial surface. Then there is a
countable subset $D\subseteq Q$ with:

**(a)** $D\cap\bar j(\Sigma)$ is dense in $\bar j(\Sigma)$; and

**(b)** $D$ is dense in $Q$.

Moreover $D$ can be chosen of the following explicit form: with
$D_0:=S_0$ a countable dense subset of $\bar j(\Sigma)$, and having chosen
for every $x\in D_n$ a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ and defined
$$V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}:=\Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^4q_ie_i(x):\ q_i\in\mathbb Q\Bigr\},$$
one sets
$$D_{n+1}:=D_n\cup\bigl\{\exp_x(v):\ x\in D_n,\ v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}\text{ timelike, with }\exp_x(v)\text{ defined}\bigr\},\qquad D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ and the member maps
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as in
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d): $Q$ is a Hausdorff locally
Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, the
open sets $Q_\alpha$ cover $Q$, and each $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$
is a diffeomorphism onto $Q_\alpha$. Let $D\subseteq Q$ be a countable dense
subset, as supplied by [[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]]. Then $Q$ is
second countable ([[def-second-countable-space]]).

More precisely, the family
$$\mathcal B:=\Bigl\{\exp_x\bigl(B(0;r)\bigr):\ x\in D,\ r\in\mathbb Q_{>0},\ B(0;r)\subseteq W_x\Bigr\},$$
where $W_x$ is the star-shaped exponential domain of a strictly convex normal
chart at $x$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] clause (a)) and $B(0;r)$
is the coordinate ball of radius $r$ in $T_xQ$ in that chart, is a countable
basis of the topology of $Q$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

derivations.claim: (One exponential step produces the rational points with nonzero time coordinate.) In the standard coordinates the exponential map is $\exp_d(v)=d+v$ ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]: geodesics are straight lines with affine parameter in flat coordinates). For $d=(0,q)\in\mathbb Q^3\times\{0\}=D_0$ and a rational vector $v=(a,w)\in\mathbb Q^4$ the point $d+v=(a,q+w)$ lies in $D_1$ whenever $v$ is timelike, i.e. $a^2<|w|^2$. Given $(a,b)\in\mathbb Q^4$ with $a\ne0$, choose $q:=b$ and $w:=0$; then $v=(a,0)$ satisfies $\eta(v,v)=-a^2<0$, so it is timelike, and $(a,b)\in D_1$. Hence $\{r\in\mathbb Q^4:\ r^0\ne0\}\subseteq D_1$, and $D_0$ supplies the points with $r^0=0$, so $\mathbb Q^4\subseteq D$.

(Countability and density.) $D$ is countable by the construction ([[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]], [[def-countable]]) and contains $\mathbb Q^4$, which is dense in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ by the density of $\mathbb Q$ in $\mathbb R$ coordinatewise ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]); hence $D$ is dense and meets $j(\Sigma)=\{t=0\}$ in $\mathbb Q^3\times\{0\}$.

(The basis.) For $d\in D$ and rational $r>0$ the set $\exp_d(B(0;r))=d+B(0;r)$ is the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ around $d$ centred at a rational point with rational radius; the family of all such balls is a countable basis of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-topology-basis-subbasis]], [[def-second-countable-space]]). In particular $\mathcal B$ as defined in the statement is a countable basis of the topology of $M$, so $M$ is second countable, in accordance with [[lem-gr-development-quotient-second-countable]].
